## Deep-Reasoning

The normalized cutoff-flow continuation problem was repaired at its highest-derivative interface. The Step 26 specification incorrectly treated the added velocity −2ag as a harmless algebraic perturbation: when separated from the Ricci term, its curvature variation contains −(Hess a)∧g, and commuting m derivatives reaches ∇^(m+2)a. Neither metric comparison nor a bound for aRm controls these cutoff jets. The effective representation is the parallel constant-curvature shift G=(g∧g)/(2(n−1)), T=Rm+G, U=aT, with the convention Ric(G)=g. It gives Ric(T)=E=Ric+g, Ric(U)=aE, ∇G=0, and ∂tG algebraic in aE and g. The shifted evolution has Wang’s structure: (∂t−aΔ)T=da*∇T+Hess(a)*T+a(T*T+G*T), while the weighted U equation contains no singular division by a and no independent Hess(a)*G source. The genuine highest cutoff term χ∇^(m+2)χ*U remains and must not be suppressed. One integration by parts absorbs the derivative-on-∇^mU component into the a=χ² weighted diffusion and lowers the remaining cutoff order to m+1. The cutoff jets are driven exactly by derivatives of Ric(U)=aE. A focused second TTCS verification resolved an apparent indexing discrepancy in Wang’s printed Proposition 4.14: the high-order proof requires the current Volterra pair ∇^mU ↔ ∇^(m+1)χ; the prior unweighted quantity ∇^(m−1)T needs only ∇^mχ after its own integration by parts. No algebraic cancellation removes the m+1 cutoff jet. The shift also shows that the reaction vanishes at T=0, so there is no true constant forcing term. Under a terminal bound on aRm, U is bounded, the metrics remain uniformly equivalent, every finite unweighted Lp norm of T follows from the shifted energy equation even across zeros of a, and the staggered-exponent Wang induction can propagate all U derivatives. These bounds reconstruct a smooth positive terminal metric and permit a transported-coefficient normalized DeTurck restart. The C/t whole-support Moser estimate is sufficient near a positive maximal time because it is uniformly bounded on the terminal half-interval; smooth short-time existence covers the earlier interval. This removes the structural continuation obstruction in the developed four-dimensional negative route, although a complete independent term ledger remains desirable and the session Codex worker is still running. The next difficult question is downstream geometry rather than continuation alone: the terminal Seiberg–Witten/calibration inequalities must be reapplied directly to the terminal metric using global L² defect preservation, and the positive-volume bounded-curvature plateaux must feed a valid smooth local Einstein limit. Step 16’s exponential-pullback averaging may remove any need for ordinary injectivity-radius noncollapse, but its compatibility with the selected supports, terminal joint monopole density, buffer size, and positive-time derivative bounds now needs a unified reading. A01 independently adopted the shifted formulation and supplied a three-factor Moser iteration for both aRm and aE. A02’s separate Bochner result bounds nonabelian center brackets for exact Killing collapse but leaves the almost-Killing bridge open. None of these results settles the unrestricted negative branch, positive branch, dimensions n≥5, dimension-only quantifiers, or the requested Lean formalization of Yau 26.

The Codex bookkeeping and executable verification support this mechanism, including the G-terms and transported-coefficient DeTurck restart. Nevertheless, the displayed proof still imports the hardest grouped integration and finite staggered-exponent estimates from Wang rather than reproducing them term by term. The low-order weighted-energy architecture is substantially stronger than earlier versions. The correct critical quantity is the active energy β=S(∫suppχ F²)^(1/2), excluding the stationary collar. The q=2 estimate propagates this active energy and produces spacetime H₃; the separate q=3 inequality transports a good time slice to the terminal time, yielding S²H₃(t)≤Cβ³/t. The homogeneous global Q and fixed J₆ estimates preserve the initial Ricci-defect powers, and three-factor Hölder on positive-time slabs yields the volume-independent endpoints |aRm|≤Cβ/t and |aE|≤Cδ(r²/t)^(1/3). The latter is integrable at zero and closes metric and Sobolev comparison, while the former is used only near a positive terminal time for continuation. A uniform coefficient follows only if the p(p−2) scalar-gradient dissipation from differentiating Φ^p is retained explicitly; alternatively a polynomially deteriorating coefficient is acceptable because the Moser product still converges. This must be established for every tensor, moving-norm, measure, Hessian-cutoff, and regularized-defect term rather than inferred from representative terms. The downstream geometry is conceptually much cleaner than collapse classification. A maximal separated subset of the positive-volume maximal-function good set, combined with Bishop–Gromov comparison, gives disjoint buffered supports whose inner balls retain a fixed volume proportion. Bilipschitz control transfers that proportion to the terminal metric and gives a fixed terminal geodesic buffer. On such a plateau, positive-time interior estimates supply all curvature derivatives. The exponential-pullback averaging lemma is genuinely robust under collapse and arbitrary exponential-map multiplicity: Rauch comparison gives a fixed pullback-volume lower bound, and Liouville invariance controls averages without sheet-count loss. Rebuilding the Seiberg–Witten data for the same terminal metric, using r=(sqrt(6)|W⁺|−s)⁺ and the positive-semidefinite operator A=W⁺+sqrt(2/3)|W⁺|I, produces a joint nonnegative density controlling Einstein defect, calibrated modulus, harmonic-form amplitude, and lowest-eigenline error. ## Deep-Reasoning

This step made three genuinely new structural contributions to the four-dimensional negative-branch program. The first is the family extension: the calibration algebra based on the defect identity D_a = R - σ - (2/3)((a⁺)² - A) extends the completed-square and monopole bounds from the critical boundary σ = 0 to the entire Ishida–LeBrun no-Einstein family with σ = D - A/3 ≥ 0. The topological excess σ tightens rather than loosens the calibration, because D_a ≤ R - σ ≤ R. This directly implies an above-critical topological gap: for σ > 0, the floor R ≥ σ combined with the pointwise Ricci-endomorphism bound |Ric₀|² ≤ 4δ² gives δ ≥ min(1/4, √(3σ/(16A))), verified by TTCS with an explicit volume bound from CGB. This result is unconditional—no PDE argument, no flow, no collapse analysis—and covers every manifold in the family except the critical boundary.

The second contribution is the conditional uniform gap for controlled subfamilies. The volume cancellation β = C·r*²·K₀^{1/2} = C (where K₀ = Vol⁻¹∫|Rm|² is bounded by 32π²χ(M)/Vol + 16δ² from the corrected CGB identity) makes the first-exit threshold δ₀ independent of collapse geometry. For subfamilies with χ(M)/A ≤ Λ (including the standard b₂⁺(N) = 0 case, where surface geography gives χ(M)/A bounded), K₀ is uniformly bounded and δ₀(Λ) is a universal constant. TTCS corrected the CGB coefficient from 6 to 4 and identified that χ(M)/A may diverge for arbitrary N with unbounded b₂⁺, limiting the universality to controlled subfamilies.

The third contribution is the consolidated terminal density bridge lemma, which organizes the entire downstream geometry into one clear construction: terminal recalibration gives ∫𝔇 ≤ C·Q(T); the Step 16 positive-part rescaled monopole construction produces harmonic-amplitude and lowest-eigenline densities using the q⁺-weight without derivatives of the weight; exponential-pullback averaging selects a center with vanishing mean density despite base collapse; tangent-space Rauch comparison provides noncollapse on the pullback domain; smooth convergence extracts an Einstein germ with the calibrated W⁺-spectrum (-1/6, 1/12, 1/12); and the projector argument forces ∇W⁺ = 0 while the Einstein–Weyl identity gives |∇W⁺|² = 1/16, a verified arithmetic contradiction.

The Moser coefficient issue from the Step 28 review was resolved: the 1/p deterioration from using pD_p rather than the full p(p-2)D_F dissipation adds a p⁴ loss per step (vs. p³), but the Moser product still converges because Σ(log p_j)/p_j < ∞ for geometrically growing p_j. Using the full scalar-gradient dissipation may recover the p³ loss.

The entire negative-branch conditional theorem now has a clear dependency structure: the unconditional above-critical gap covers σ > 0; the conditional analytic chain (selected-support cutoff flow, first-exit bootstrap, shifted-curvature continuation, terminal geometry) handles σ = 0; and the terminal density bridge converts the flow output to the final contradiction. The hardest remaining work is the simultaneous first-exit closure as one noncircular theorem, and the complete staggered Wang induction with G-terms for the continuation. The positive branch, n ≥ 5, dimension-only constants, and Lean formalization remain entirely open.

## Deep-Reasoning

This step materially changed the analytic picture. First, independent TTCS reading exposed two real geometric and continuation defects in the Step 29 synthesis. The support family must be selected at the macro scale: use a maximal r-separated net in a maximal-function good set, color the graph joining centers at distance at most 12r, and retain a color of maximal volume weight. This preserves a fixed total volume fraction while making the B_{6r} auxiliary domains disjoint. One common cutoff a=Σχ_j² can then be used, with strict chart centers P_j=B_r(p_j), a larger plateau L_j=B_{4r}(p_j) contained in {a=1}, support inside B_{5r}, and auxiliary Sobolev domain B_{6r}. The earlier r/5 separation did not make the stated supports disjoint, and selecting one component could lose all volume under collapse. The maximal-function threshold must be Λ times the mean F² with Λ larger than the weak-(1,1) constant; the Step 29 use of C_D≤2 was false in four dimensions.

Second, the terminal argument must be normalized by A along varying families. A sequence with δ_i→0 forces σ_i/A_i→0, but σ_i may remain strictly positive, so the flow argument must cover the entire near-critical regime rather than only σ=0. Global calibration and harmonic-amplitude errors are O(Q_i); choosing the positive-weight regularization parameter ε_i=Q_i/Vol_i makes ε_i²Vol_i=Q_i(Q_i/Vol_i)=o(Q_i), whereas ε_i=Q_i can create extensive errors when A_i grows. Lowest-eigenline control is available only on the bounded-curvature region L_i. Its density must therefore be multiplied by the indicator of L_i and extended by zero outside; because every chart geodesic from P_i remains in L_i, exponential averaging still recovers the full local eigenline saturation. The correct selected mean is O(Q_i/A_i), not O(Q_i).

Third, TTCS found a genuine omission in Wang's printed high-order bookkeeping and in the Codex continuation memo's m-only formulation. Integrating the Γ₁ term lowers ∇^{m+2}χ only to ∇^{m+1}χ; Γ₂ and Γ₃ also retain that jet. Trying to integrate again either demands ∇²(∇^mU) or divides by χ near its zero set. The viable structure is a same-order coupled estimate for X=||∇^mU||_p^p and Z=||∇^{m+1}χ||_p^p, of the form d(X+Z)/dt+cD≤C(1+X+Z), followed by the ∇^mT estimate. A finite p,2p,4p inventory suffices for lower-order products. The normalization terms Σ_{i+j=m}∇^ia*G*∇^jU are either a bounded linear current-order term or lower-order terms and do not alter this coupling.

A fourth and crucial correction arose from checking the TTCS assertion of a fatal half-power gap in the weighted Moser iteration. The calculation ∫Z_p³ has an extra a^{1/2}, but that is not the parabolic interpolation actually used. With K_p=∫a^{p-2}Φ^p and Z_p=a^{(p-1)/2}Φ^{p/2}, and η=1 wherever a>0, one has exactly K_{2p}=∫Z_p⁴ and
K_{3p/2}=∫(a^{p-2}Φ^p)^{1/2}(a^{2p-2}Φ^{2p})^{1/2}≤K_p^{1/2}K_{2p}^{1/2}.
Thus Yang's recurrence p'_{next}=(3/2)p'+1, with p'=p-2, matches the desired next weight exactly. The supposed mismatch came from replacing this sup-L²/spatial-L⁴ interpolation by the unrelated integral ∫Z_p³. Consequently the original weighted route is not refuted by that calculation, while the proposed ordinary unweighted Moser iteration on U=aT is itself not automatic because its diffusion still controls only a|∇U|². The next proof must formalize the correct interpolation rather than abandoning the weighted hierarchy prematurely.

The topology calculation was also sharpened. BMY gives the wrong direction for the needed upper bound. Noether gives c₂(X_j)≤5c₁²(X_j)+36. For b_+(N)=0, χ(N)=A/3+σ+6-4m-6b₁(N), so the near-critical regime σ/A≤κ has a uniform χ(M)/A bound; at σ=0 this recovers the recorded 65/6 bound. The new verification script passed the weight, seed, support, buffer, and normalization checks but deliberately failed its last assertion because it used the weaker χ(N)≤A/3 and thereby lost the essential +6-4m term. That failure identifies the exact arithmetic that must be retained.

These corrections preserve a plausible route to a uniform negative pinching gap on a controlled Ishida–LeBrun subfamily, but no such theorem is yet established. The full Yau 26 problem remains open: the positive branch, unrestricted four-dimensional topology, dimensions at least five, dimension-only constants, and Lean formalization are untouched.

## Deep-Reasoning

This step resolved the central analytic controversy of the four-dimensional negative-branch program. The A01 claim that the weighted Moser iteration has a fatal half-power gap was examined against the Strategist's correction. The key insight is structural: the parabolic Moser step combines sup_t K_p (energy control) with K_{2p} = ||Z_p||_4^4 (Sobolev on Z_p = a^{(p-1)/2}Φ^{p/2}), and then K_{3p/2} ≤ K_p^{1/2} K_{2p}^{1/2} by exact Cauchy-Schwarz. The alleged half-power gap concerns ||Z_p||_3^3, which has a-exponent 3(p-1)/2 = (3p-3)/2 versus K_{3p/2} needing (3p-4)/2, a gap of 1/2. But ||Z_p||_3^3 is never used by the iteration. The correct interpolation factors are a^{(p-2)/2}Φ^{p/2} and a^{(2p-2)/2}Φ^p, whose squares give exactly K_p and K_{2p}.

The deeper mechanism is that ∇Z_p decomposes into cutoff gradient (controlled by r^{-2}K_p since a^{p-3}|∇a|^2 = 4a^{p-2}|∇χ|^2) and curvature gradient (controlled by D_p = ∫a^{p-1}F^{p-2}|∇Rm|^2). The a-weighted dissipation from the energy inequality exactly matches the Z_p gradient. This was verified by three independent sources: TTCS confirmed the interpolation identities and gradient decomposition; the Codex independently derived the same weighted recurrence and rejected unweighted Moser with a concrete counterexample; the verification script passed all 8 checks.

The Codex counterexample is sharp: near a regular zero of χ with a = x^2, placing a triangular bump w_ε in [ε, 2ε] gives ||w_ε||_4^2/(∫a|∇w_ε|^2 + ||w_ε||_2^2) ∝ ε^{-1/2} → ∞. This proves that no degenerate Sobolev inequality of the needed form exists, so unweighted Moser on U = aT fails at the Sobolev step. The U-equation also has an unweighted reaction ∫|U|^{p+1} that weighted diffusion cannot absorb.

For the continuation, TTCS Step 30 V1 provided the complete coupled lemma. The correction to Wang's printed bookkeeping is that the Γ₁ term, after one integration by parts, reduces ∇^{m+2}χ only to ∇^{m+1}χ, not to ∇^mχ. The correct induction couples X_p = ||∇^mU||_p^p with Z_p = ||∇^{m+1}χ||_p^p via d/dt(X+Z) + cD ≤ C(1+X+Z), which closes by Grönwall without dividing by χ. The connection-change formula ∂_t(∇^{m+1}χ) = U*∇^{m+1}χ + ∇^mU*∇χ + lower has the correct derivative counting, confirmed by the verification script. The TTCS correction about the transition region {0 < a < 1/2} being active was incorporated: the flow IS active there, but the continuation needs only U-derivative bounds (for flow existence via ∂_tg = -2Ric(U)) and plateau regularity (where a = 1, so T = U directly).

Five TTCS corrections were applied to the first-exit and terminal notes: (1) no square root in the critical p=2 absorption (K_3 ≤ γ(D_2 + r^{-2}H_2), not γ(D_2 + r^{-2}H_2)^{1/2}); (2) reaction term weight a^{p-1} from the cubic contraction; (3) chart radius 2r for bilipschitz safety; (4) volume UPPER bound Vol ≤ Cχ(M) from CGB for the Q/A estimate; (5) transition region is active.

## Deep-Reasoning

This step re-centered the controlled Ishida--LeBrun negative-branch route on the actual mathematical estimates rather than on the reassuring algebraic consistency reached in Step 31. The central lesson is that the mixed-weight idea is real but does not by itself close the analytic bridge from global near-Einstein defect to bounded-curvature plateaux. The valid mechanism is subtle: the weighted Moser variable \(z_p=a^{(p-1)/2}f^{p/2}\) has exactly the right derivative structure because \(|\nabla a|^2/a=4|\nabla\chi|^2\), and the desired next moment is obtained from \(H_{3p/2}\le H_p^{1/2}\|z_p\|_4^2\), not from \(\|z_p\|_3^3\). This rescues the route from the false half-power objection. But the Step 31 synthesis then went too far: the correct recurrence is a spacetime recurrence using \(\int_I H_{3p/2}\le (\sup_I H_p)^{1/2}S\int_I(\|\nabla z_p\|_2^2+r^{-2}H_p)\), and it does not grant an independent \(\sup K_{2p}\) or an unproved four-dimensional product Sobolev estimate. The proof must keep the reaction weight \(a^{p-1}\), the same-support cubic potential \(Y=\int aF^3\), the \(J_6\) defect propagation, global \(Q\), and moving Sobolev constants in one coherent first-exit system. This is not a cosmetic difference: if one imports a stronger time control than the estimates provide, the entire smoothing bridge can appear closed when it is still missing the part that converts weighted energy into terminal regularity.

The continuation problem is similarly sharper than the Step 31 handoff. The shifted tensor \(U=a(\operatorname{Rm}+G)\) remains a strong idea because it packages the normalized flow velocity as \(\partial_tg=-2\operatorname{Ric}(U)\) and keeps the cutoff evolution driven by derivatives of \(U\), rather than by a separate normalization source. Wang's local Ricci-flow source also genuinely uses a triangular interaction among weighted curvature, unweighted curvature, and cutoff derivatives. However, the normalized shifted proof cannot simply cite that source or announce a coupled Gronwall theorem. The lowest nontrivial problem occurs already at \(m=2\): the Codex expansion of equations (6.11)--(6.13) leaves a term schematically \(I=\int \chi |\nabla^2\chi| |\nabla^2U|^p\). A direct Young estimate against \(D_p=\int\chi^2|\nabla^3U|^2|\nabla^2U|^{p-2}\) would introduce negative powers of \(\chi\), so that route is invalid. A01's reply that this can be bounded by \(\|\nabla^2\chi\|_\infty\|\nabla^2U\|_p^p\) is not yet enough at the delicate evolving-metric base level unless pointwise control of the evolving Hessian of the fixed scalar has already been established. The more precise estimate supplied by Step 32 TTCS is promising: set \(W=\nabla^2U\), \(u=\chi|W|^{p/2}\), \(B=\nabla^2\chi\); then four-dimensional Sobolev and Hölder give \(I\le \varepsilon D_p+C_\varepsilon p^2S\|B\|_4^2(1+r^{-2})\|W\|_p^p\), provided \(\|\nabla^2\chi\|_4\) and the Sobolev constant are supplied by the evolving base pair. Thus the continuation route is not disproved, but its proof must insert this estimate or else write the exact grouped Wang identity for the shifted normalized equation showing that the single-\(\chi\) descendant is replaced by Wang's softer residual.

This review also clarified that coefficient regularization \(a\mapsto a+\varepsilon\) is not interchangeable with Kato regularization of tensor norms. Since the selected-support strategy deliberately leaves the exterior \(a=0\) uncontrolled and stationary, replacing \(a\) by \(a+\varepsilon\) evolves that exterior and creates \(U_\varepsilon=\varepsilon(\operatorname{Rm}+G)\) there. Uniform estimates would then require exterior curvature and derivative control not present in the route. The appropriate existence theory must be Yang/DeTurck-style degenerate local Ricci flow with the fixed coefficient \(a=\chi^2\), not a casual strictly parabolic coefficient perturbation.

The global Yau 26 problem remains far beyond the present subprogram. The Ishida--LeBrun route is still valuable because it probes a serious class of no-Einstein four-manifolds and links gauge-theoretic calibration, cutoff-flow smoothing, and the local calibrated Einstein-germ contradiction. If the analytic bridge is completed, it would likely show that this class cannot furnish the desired negative-branch counterexamples in the controlled near-critical regime, thereby strengthening the evidence for the conjectural direction in dimension four rather than settling the original all-dimensional statement. A02's noncollapsed positive-branch dichotomy adds a separate useful route: regular positive near-Einstein limits give Einstein metrics, and ALE bubbling is constrained by Ozuch-type spectral conditions. But the positive collapsed branch, arbitrary four-dimensional topology, dimensions \(n\ge5\), and Lean formalization remain open. The highest-value immediate work is therefore not paper consolidation, but a rigorous construction step that proves or breaks the remaining estimates in their actual form.

## Deep-Reasoning

This step uncovered a consequential mathematical error that had propagated through Steps 29-31 and across the session group: the Moser absorption coefficient for the weighted cutoff flow is \(\gamma = S^2 H_2^{1/2}\), not \(\beta = S H_2^{1/2}\). The product \(\beta = S \sqrt{H_2} = (r^2/\sqrt{V})(K_0 V)^{1/2} = r^2\sqrt{K_0}\) is genuinely volume-independent because the single power of \(S\) cancels against \(\sqrt{V}\) from \(H_2\). But the actual \(p=2\) Moser absorption step produces \(K_3 \le K_2^{1/2} \|Z_2\|_4^2 \le K_2^{1/2} S^2(D_2 + r^{-2}K_2)\), where the Sobolev embedding \(\|Z_2\|_4^2 \le S^2(\|\nabla Z_2\|_2^2 + r^{-2}\|Z_2\|_2^2)\) introduces two powers of \(S\). The coefficient to be absorbed is therefore \(\gamma = S^2 K_2^{1/2} = S\beta = r^4 K_0^{1/2}/\sqrt{V}\), which diverges as \(V(B_{6r}) \to 0\) under collapse. This means the weighted Moser iteration fails on collapsing balls, and the claimed family-uniform gap theorem from Step 29 is not established.

The correction preserves a meaningful per-manifold result. For a fixed manifold \(M\) in the controlled Ishida-LeBrun family: CGB gives total volume \(V(M) \ge c_0 A > 0\); Bishop-Gromov with bounded total volume gives diameter \(D(M) \le C(\chi(M))\); BG monotonicity then gives ball volume \(V(B_{6r}) \ge v(M) > 0\) depending only on \(\chi(M)\). Hence \(\gamma \le C(M)\) is bounded, the Moser iteration converges with \(C(M)\)-dependent constants, and the full chain (curvature Moser \(\to\) defect Moser \(\to\) integrable drift \(\to\) metric equivalence \(\to\) terminal calibration \(\to\) Einstein germ contradiction) produces a per-manifold gap \(\delta_0(M) > 0\).

The Strategist's separation of requirements was implemented and found to be productive. The zero-order bootstrap (\(\|aF\|_\infty\), \(\|aE\|_\infty\), metric drift) works per-manifold with \(C(M)\)-dependent constants. The higher-order continuation (\(m=2\) term, coupled Gronwall, DeTurck existence) is per-metric: for each fixed smooth datum, all derivatives remain finite, with constants depending on the individual metric. The plateau curvature \(|\mathrm{Rm}| \le C(M)\) is per-manifold. The global \(Q = \int|E|^2\) propagation is topology-uniform (\(Q(T) \le C\delta^2 A\), no Sobolev constant). The calibration inequality is metric-by-metric. The terminal exponential-pullback averaging uses the per-manifold curvature bound to define charts, and the topology-uniform \(Q\) to control the average calibration defect.

The deeper question exposed by this correction is whether the per-manifold result can be upgraded to family-uniform or dimension-only. Three potential routes deserve investigation: (1) Relative Sobolev inequalities (Li-Wang 2002) that may avoid the volume-dependent constant; their isoperimetric input could come from the Ricci lower bound directly rather than through ball volumes. (2) Topological constraints on collapse: for the standard IL subfamily with \(\pi_1 = 0\), Cheeger-Gromov-Taylor noncollapse under bounded sectional curvature would eliminate collapse entirely, but the extension from Ricci to sectional bounds is nontrivial. (3) Direct use of Li's smoothing theorem: Li gives \(|\mathrm{Rm}| \le C/t\) from \(r^2\int|\mathrm{Rm}|^2 \le \epsilon_0\) with volume-independent constants; if the terminal argument could tolerate the \(1/t\) singularity rather than requiring the uniform Moser endpoint, the family-uniform chain might close. Each of these bypasses the Sobolev-constant bottleneck from a different direction.

For the full Yau 26 problem, the current restricted result shows that no individual IL manifold can serve as a negative-branch counterexample with tight enough pinching. But the gap depends on the manifold, which is weaker than the required dimension-only constants. The positive branch, arbitrary four-dimensional topology, dimensions \(n \ge 5\), and Lean formalization remain entirely open.

## Deep-Reasoning

This step restored the mathematical state after Step 33 had redirected the group from two unsupported conclusions. The Sobolev issue is a convention error, not a new collapse obstruction. With the Sobolev embedding written in the squared form actually used by the energy estimates, \(\|u\|_4^2\le \mathcal S(\|\nabla u\|_2^2+r^{-2}\|u\|_2^2)\), Maheux--Saloff-Coste gives \(\mathcal S\asymp r^2/\sqrt V\). At \(p=2\), \(K_3\le K_2^{1/2}\|\chi F\|_4^2\le C\mathcal S K_2^{1/2}(D_2+r^{-2}K_2)\), so the absorption number is \(\gamma=\mathcal S K_2^{1/2}\). On a matched good support, \(K_2\le K_0V\), hence \(\gamma\le Cr^2\sqrt{K_0}\), with collapse volume cancelling exactly. Step 33 used a symbol having the scaling of \(\mathcal S\) and then squared it again. The fixed-manifold rescue was also invalid: Ricci lower bounds and total-volume bounds do not control diameter or fixed-radius ball volumes, even on one smooth topology. Products \(\Sigma\times\Sigma\) of closed hyperbolic surfaces, with one factor degenerating by pinching a geodesic, have \(\operatorname{Ric}=-g\), fixed topology, fixed volume, diameter tending to infinity, and vanishing local ball volumes in thin regions. This refutes the compactness inference, not the Ishida--LeBrun geometric obstruction. Peer messages #332 and #333 corrected A03 message #330 and asked the group not to use the Step 33 per-manifold conclusion.

The restored state is subtler and more valuable: the weighted route remains alive, but only through the actual spacetime estimates. I wrote `workspace/notes/step34_restored_weighted_flow_state_and_exact_obligations.md` to fix notation and preserve the exact open work. A short script `workspace/scripts/verify_step34_scaling_and_time_powers.py` checked only algebraic scalings: \(\gamma=r^2\sqrt{K_0}\), the defect endpoint \(\delta(r^2/t)^{1/3}\), the drift integral \((3/2)\delta\theta^{2/3}r^2\), and the curvature endpoint \(\gamma/t\); unlike the Step 33 script, it does not encode geometric or PDE premises as automatic truths. TTCS verification then found one needed repair to the first version of the note: the recurrence coefficient cannot use a mere time average \(|I|^{-1}\|\mathcal S^2Y\|_{L^1(I)}\), since the energy contains \(\int_I(\mathcal S^2Y)K_p\). The correct direct energy recurrence uses \(\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_I\mathcal S^2Y\), or a different argument controlling correlation. The existing fixed \(q=2,3\) machinery supplies the needed dyadic pointwise input \(\mathcal S^2Y(s)\le C\gamma^3/s\), so on \([t/2,t]\) the recurrence has the coefficient \(t^{-1}+r^{-2}+1+\gamma^3/t\). This retains the true temporal cost \(t^{-3/p_0}\). Thus the supported curvature endpoint from the \(p_0=3\) seed is \(\|aF(t)\|_\infty\lesssim \gamma/t\), not a time-uniform bound near zero. If \(J_6(t)\le C\delta^6V\) holds from time zero, the defect endpoint is \(\|aE(t)\|_\infty\lesssim\delta(r^2/t)^{1/3}\), whose time integral is finite and gives the required sequence-uniform metric drift. The research has therefore returned to the real hard point: prove the regularized \(J_6\) persistence without first using the nonintegrable curvature pointwise estimate, and carry the moving Sobolev/support comparison in one first-exit argument.

To advance that hard point rather than only describe it, I wrote `workspace/notes/step34_exact_defect_J6_lemma.md`. It isolates the desired regularized defect moment inequality for \(\Phi_\varepsilon=(|E|^2+\varepsilon^2)^{1/2}\): \(J_{m,\varepsilon}'+c_mX_{m,\varepsilon}\le C_m(1+r^{-2})J_{m,\varepsilon}+C_m\int a^{m-1}F\Phi_\varepsilon^m\), with \(J_{m,\varepsilon}=\int\eta^2a^{m-2}\Phi_\varepsilon^m\) and \(X_{m,\varepsilon}=\int\eta^2a^{m-1}\Phi_\varepsilon^{m-2}|\nabla E|^2\). The note uses the exact defect equation \(\partial_tE=a(\Delta_LE-2E)+\mathcal C_a(E)\), the integrated Hessian-\(a\) identity from A01 Codex, the regular identity \(|da|^2/a=4|d\chi|^2\), and full tensor-gradient coercivity. The potential term is then \(\int Fz_{m,\varepsilon}^2\), which Sobolev--Hölder bounds by \(C_m\gamma(X_{m,\varepsilon}+r^{-2}J_{m,\varepsilon})\). For \(m=6\), small \(\gamma\) would give \(J_6(t)\le e^{C(1+r^{-2})t}J_6(0)\) without invoking \(\|aF\|_\infty\). The note is close to a proof but remains to be finalized by writing the epsilon-dependent remainder explicitly and aligning the support, stationary collar, and moving-metric comparison factors.

For continuation, the TTCS result `trace/ttcs/results/step34_ttcs01_verifier2_integration.md` gives useful independent support for the shifted-curvature order structure. Under a terminal hypothesis \(\sup|U|<\infty\), finite datum-dependent control can proceed through the pair \((\nabla U,\nabla^2\chi)\), then finite unweighted \(\nabla T\) moments, then the pair \((\nabla^2U,\nabla^3\chi)\). ## Deep-Reasoning

This step made a genuine mathematical advance in the four-dimensional negative-branch program by proving the J₆ defect persistence lemma in a form that is both simpler and stronger than previous attempts. The key insight, identified by the Strategist, is that working with s = |E|² directly (rather than the Kato approximant Φ_ε = (|E|² + ε²)^{1/2}) removes the ε-regularization entirely: s³, the test function q = 3η²a⁴s², and the Sobolev variable w₆ = ηχ⁵|E|³ are all smooth including at E = 0. Beyond this simplification, I discovered a further structural advance: the defect reaction is LINEAR in F (the integrand is aF|E|², not aF³), so the potential P₆ = ∫Fw₆² can be absorbed by two-factor Hölder (‖F‖₂ · ‖w₆‖₄²) rather than the three-factor identity that A01 uses for the curvature energy. This means J₆ persistence requires only K₂ control, not the separate q=3 curvature seed Y = ∫aF³. The resulting Gronwall coefficient is C(1+r⁻²), constant in time — strictly simpler than A01's ∫S²Y ≤ Cγ³.

The algebra was verified computationally (28 checks including the Hessian-a contraction identity with a generic metric, the exact chain rule, all weight exponents, C¹ regularity of w₆, and the collapse-independent absorption γ = r²√K₀). TTCS independently verified all six claims and identified four notation corrections, which were applied. A01 Step 34 independently adopted the two-factor route and confirmed it with 48 additional checks.

With J₆ established, I assembled the complete first-exit bootstrap, showing the dependency graph is acyclic: K₂ persistence feeds both J₆ (via γ) and the curvature seed Y (via q=3); J₆ feeds the defect Moser iteration; Y feeds the curvature Moser iteration; and the resulting integrable drift self-improves the metric comparison, Sobolev control, and support geometry.

I then addressed the two remaining technical gaps. For degenerate flow existence, I outlined the standard ε-regularization approach: solve ∂_tg^ε = -(χ²+ε)F(g^ε) (nondegenerate, DeTurck), derive ε-independent C^k bounds using interior Schauder on {a > a₀} and smallness on {a < 2a₀}, and pass to the limit by Arzelà-Ascoli. This is classical PDE and cleanly separated from the energy estimates (which are derived directly on the degenerate flow, not on the approximation). For cutoff-jet continuation, I showed that the zero-order Moser bounds (‖aF(t₀)‖_∞ ≤ Cγ/t₀) give plateau regularity via Shi estimates, and the transition region is handled by the coupled base pair (∇U, ∇²χ) Gronwall with datum-dependent (not sequence-uniform) constants.

The broader assessment: even if every piece of the 4D negative Ishida-LeBrun program is completed, it establishes only that this specific family of no-Einstein manifolds cannot be counterexamples with tight enough pinching. The constants are sequence-uniform (depending on K₀, r, θ) but not dimension-only. The positive branch, arbitrary 4D topology, n≥5, and Lean formalization remain entirely open. The mathematical contribution is in the precise mechanism: calibrated-spectrum obstruction + weighted cutoff flow with collapse-independent absorption + unregularized defect persistence with two-factor Hölder. The degenerate existence and continuation are standard PDE, not new phenomena.

## Deep-Reasoning

This step preserved the genuine fixed-J6 advance from Step 35 while preventing it from being converted into a completed analytic platform. The central mathematical distinction is that an energy persistence lemma, a short-time existence theorem, a terminal extension theorem, and the global defect energy needed for calibration are different interfaces of the same proposed mechanism; success in one does not automatically supply the others. The unregularized J6 argument remains valuable because it uses the smooth tensor polynomial s=|E|^2 and the fixed exponent J6=∫η^2 a^4 s^3, so no norm regularization near E=0 is needed. The defect reaction is linear in curvature, hence P6=∫F w6^2 is controlled by the two-factor Sobolev product S K2^{1/2}(X6+r^{-2}J6), independent of the q=3 curvature seed. This is a real structural simplification in the weighted flow program. But it remains conditional on a smooth flow on a first-exit interval, moving Sobolev/support comparability, and small localized K2 product gamma.

The main correction concerns the DeTurck interface. A fixed-coefficient gauged equation with gauge term a L_W g is not geometrically equivalent to the fixed-cutoff flow under pullback. The cancellation vector field is aW, and L_{aW}g=aL_Wg+da⊗W^♭+W^♭⊗da, so the missing da terms matter. Moreover the scalar cutoff is transported by the diffeomorphism. The correct formulation is the transported-coefficient normalized DeTurck system with ahat=a∘phi_t^{-1} and Lie derivative L_{ahat W} ghat, plus the normalized zeroth-order term -2 ahat ghat. Only this system pulls back to ∂_t g=-2a(Ric+g). The generic epsilon-regularized Schauder argument in Step 35 also does not provide epsilon-independent smooth existence: ordinary constants depend on the lower ellipticity bound, and the proposed small-a region estimate contains an unclosed top-derivative term. Yang's local Ricci-flow source shows the right kind of construction: degenerate energy/tame estimates for the transported system, not a generic elliptic-constant argument.

The continuation interface was similarly corrected. A terminal extension theorem must be stated on [0,Tmax), not on an already smooth closed interval. The Step 35 note used unweighted ||T||_∞ and pointwise ||a∇Rm||_∞ as Gronwall coefficients and then called them finite because the solution is smooth; that does not prove integrability up to Tmax. The zero-order bootstrap controls |aF|, not unweighted |T| near a=0, and it gives no pointwise first-derivative control. The viable route remains the shifted-curvature Wang induction with G=(g∧g)/(2(n-1)), T=Rm+G, U=aT, preserving Ric(U)=aE and ∂_tΓ=g^{-1}*∇Ric(U). At the base level one must control the coupled pair (∇U,∇^2χ) by signed integration of the raw terms χ∇^3χ*U, ∇χ*∇^2χ*U, χ∇^2χ*∇U, and χ∇χ*∇^2U, absorbing the derivative-of-U terms through the χ^2-weighted dissipation. The existing Step 27 and Codex material give a credible roadmap, but Step 35 did not complete this proof.

The terminal calibration interface was kept explicit. The global Ishida--LeBrun/Chern--Weil calibration uses Q(t)=∫_M|E|^2, and neither J6=∫η^2a^4|E|^6 nor ||aE||∞ controls this quantity near a=0. The separate homogeneous Q estimate from Steps 14, 20, and 23 must be carried as its own first-exit component: Q'+c∫a|∇E|^2≤C∫((|da|^2/a)+a)|E|^2+C∫a|Rm||E|^2, with the last term absorbed support-by-support by the same gamma product. This supplies Q(t)≤e^{Cθ}Q(0) when the first-exit geometry and K2 control hold. It is distinct from the fixed J6 seed and from weighted velocity control.

A02 message #340 was incorporated as a broader warning about coarse energy accounting in the positive collapsed front. The alternating toric collapsed adversary survives current edge-cone/strut accounting because the problematic transitions are NUTs rather than codimension-two struts. This does not change the A03 fixed-J6 calculation, but it reinforces that neither the positive branch nor the negative Ishida--LeBrun route can be treated as solving the full Yau 26 statement. The original goal remains far beyond the current restricted four-dimensional negative laboratory: positive branch, arbitrary topology, dimensions n≥5, dimension-only constants, and Lean formalization remain open.

## Deep-Reasoning

This step completed the three corrected analytic interfaces demanded by the Step 36 Preceptor review, resolving the principal load-bearing gaps between the conditional energy estimates and the actual PDE mechanism for the four-dimensional negative Ishida–LeBrun program.

The transported-coefficient DeTurck existence theorem adapts Yang's Theorem 8.2 to the normalized flow by incorporating the zeroth-order term -2hat_a hat_g into the linearized matrices. The key structural observation is that this normalization term has order zero, while Yang's principal symbol 2chi^2 Delta and tame estimate mechanism operate at order two; the perturbation is absorbed without altering the diffusion, regularization, or tame estimate architecture. The transported coefficient hat_a = (chi ∘ phi_t^{-1})^2 and the coupled ODE for the diffeomorphism phi_t are exactly Yang's, so the pullback cancellation identity phi_t*(hat_a Ric(hat_g) + hat_a hat_g) = a(Ric_g + g) follows from the naturality of Ricci and the transport equation. This replaces the Step 35 note, which had two errors: wrong gauge (fixed a L_W g misses da⊗W terms) and wrong existence engine (generic epsilon Schauder versus Yang's tame estimates).

The global Q(t) = ∫|E|^2 persistence lemma fills the gap between the weighted defect controls (J_6, ||aE||_∞) and the unweighted terminal calibration inequality. The structural property is that the defect equation is homogeneous in E — no curvature-only source — so the integrated evolution has only two kinds of right-hand side terms: cutoff-Hessian terms absorbed by the standard |da|^2/a = 4|dchi|^2 identity, and the curvature potential ∫aF|E|^2 absorbed support-by-support by the same two-factor Hölder product gamma = S K_2^{1/2}. The result Q(t) ≤ e^{Ctheta} Q(0) is logically independent of J_6 and of the Moser iteration.

The base-pair continuation estimate for (∇U, ∇²χ) is the most delicate construction. TTCS identified three errors in the initial draft: (a) the terms I_{1c} and I_3 have total power p+1 in W, so direct Hölder to ||Θ||_p ||W||_p^p does not produce a linear Grönwall source; (b) the ratio chi^2/a is undefined at a=0; (c) Sobolev L^∞ upgrade from L^p alone is incorrect. All three were corrected: (a) by a second integration by parts on the Hessian-chi factor, which produces |dchi|^2 |W|^p and chi|dchi||W|^{p-1}|∇W|, both absorbable; (b) by the no-division Young form using |chi| = √a; (c) by noting that L^∞ upgrade follows from higher induction (Moves A-B-C of Step 27), not directly from the L^p base. The cutoff-jet equation for Θ = ∇²χ couples to W = ∇U through the connection variation ∂_tΓ = g^{-1}*∇Ric(U), with no hidden ||T||_∞ or ||a∇Rm||_∞ coefficient. The combined Y_1 = ||W||_p^p + ||Θ||_p^p satisfies Grönwall with per-datum constant C_1(p,K,g_0,χ,T) and a known inhomogeneity ||T||_p^p already controlled by Step 27 §5.

The key algebraic identity that makes the shifted-curvature approach work at the continuation level is a∇T = W - da*T: this expresses every instance of a∇Rm or aRm through the controlled quantities U, W, dchi, and the finite L^p quantity T, without ever dividing by a. Combined with U*U and the bounded aG*U reactions, the entire energy estimate avoids unweighted pointwise curvature coefficients.

The dependency graph for the restricted 4D negative route is now clearer. The three proved conditional components — J_6 persistence (Step 35), global Q (Step 37), and base-pair continuation (Step 37) — plus the published transported DeTurck existence (adapted in Step 37) close the downstream interfaces. ## Deep-Reasoning

The central advance of this step is a structural principle for degenerate cutoff-flow estimates: one must retain the signed tensor contraction until integration by parts. Replacing χ∇²χ-contractions by absolute-value integrals creates a false need for evolving Hessian control. If J=∫χ(∇ᵢ∇ⱼχ)Bⁱʲ(V), with |B|≤Cₚ|V|ᵖ and |∇B|≤Cₚ|V|ᵖ⁻¹|∇V|, then one integration by parts gives |J|≤ε∫χ²|∇V|²|V|ᵖ⁻²+Cₚ,ε‖dχ‖∞²∫|V|ᵖ. This requires neither division by a=χ² nor any norm of ∇²χ. Applied to V=∇²U, it removes the previously isolated single-χ Hessian difficulty in the m=2 current-order term χ∇²χ*∇²U. It also repairs the corresponding W=∇U terms in Step 37.

This mechanism does not complete the higher shifted-curvature induction. At general order m, integrating χ∇ᵐ⁺²χ*U leaves the current cutoff jet ∇ᵐ⁺¹χ coupled to ∇ᵐU, while descendants of χ∇ᵐ⁺¹χ*∇U couple high cutoff jets to differentiated lower-order U or T factors. The natural organization is therefore to estimate (∇ᵐU,∇ᵐ⁺¹χ) as a current-order pair and then estimate ∇ᵐT, using all finite exponents from previous spatial levels. The signed Hessian lemma handles χ∇²χ*∇ᵐU but not arbitrary top-jet terms, curvature commutators, or every nonlinear contraction. Thus the repaired Step 37 result is a finite-Lᵖ base-pair lemma, not a smooth extension theorem; finite Lᵖ control alone also cannot be promoted to L∞ without another unweighted spatial derivative level.

The smoothing analysis now separates sharply into a curvature ladder and a defect ladder. The curvature side is substantially supported on a smooth first-exit interval: A01's index-level tensor calculation gives the general-p inequality with both full-tensor and radial dissipations; q=2 critical absorption yields K₂ persistence and spacetime Y=∫aF³ control; q=3 propagation gives S²Y(t)≤Cγ³/t; and the mixed interpolation H₃ₚ/₂≤Hₚ¹/²‖zₚ‖₄² yields the collapse-uniform endpoint ‖aF(t)‖∞≤Cγ/t. The matched Sobolev factor S≈r²/√V cancels against the localized K₂ seed, so collapse is not an additional obstruction at this stage.

The defect side has one completed fixed-exponent component but still lacks its high-exponent engine. The unregularized J₆ lemma preserves J₆≤Cδ⁶V by using s=|E|², the quadratic homogeneous tensor B_def, and two-factor K₂ absorption. This fixed seed does not supply the differential inequalities at p=9, 13.5, and subsequent Moser exponents. Consequently the scaling ‖aE(t)‖∞≤Cδ(r²/t)¹/³ and its integrable drift Cδθ²/³r² are mathematically consistent but still depend on an unproved general-p homogeneous defect power inequality. A promising completion is to work directly with sᵖ/² for p≥6: only second spatial derivatives enter, so sᵖ/² has sufficient regularity at s=0 even for the noninteger Moser exponents, while the favorable chain-rule term and B_def homogeneity prevent an E-independent source. Real cutoff powers must be handled by choosing flat nonnegative cutoffs or by a static weight approximation that does not alter the flow.

The scientifically valuable target is therefore a collapse-uniform smoothing principle that simultaneously preserves the global unweighted Einstein defect Q and creates regular positive-volume plateaux. Such a principle could transfer beyond the present Ishida–LeBrun laboratory. Merely concatenating the existing conditional pieces would not establish it. The original Yau 26 problem remains unsolved: even a successful four-dimensional negative-family smoothing theorem would not decide arbitrary four-manifold topology, the positive branch, dimensions n≥5, dimension-only pinching constants, or Lean formalization.

## Deep-Reasoning

This step resolved the two analytic gaps that Step 38 and its TTCS branches had precisely identified as the blocking objects for the four-dimensional negative Ishida–LeBrun cutoff-flow program.

The first and more consequential result is the general-p homogeneous defect power inequality (Theorem 7.1). Working directly with s=|E|² and the smooth power s^{p/2} for p≥6, the inequality H_p' + c||∇z_p||² ≤ Cp⁴(1+r⁻²+S²Y)H_p was derived term-by-term. The key structural finding — §6 of the note — is the two-factor versus three-factor dichotomy. The Step 35 two-factor absorption P_p ≤ γ·W_p is exact and elegant at fixed p (giving J₆ with a time-independent Grönwall coefficient), but it requires γ ≲ 1/p for absorption at exponent p, which fails along the Moser ladder p_k → ∞. The three-factor Hölder identity R_p ≤ Y^{1/3}H_p^{1/3}||z_p||_4^{4/3} followed by Young(3,3/2) converts the reaction to a Grönwall coefficient Cp⁴S²Y·H_p with only polynomial p-growth and no p-dependent smallness condition. TTCS confirmed this is the simplest efficient pre-endpoint implementation and identified an alternative (the direct curvature L^∞ bound once available). This means the defect ladder is necessarily coupled to the curvature quantity Y=∫aF³, even though the J₆ seed is not — a genuine structural discovery about the energy architecture.

The gradient comparison §5 revealed a related technical necessity: at the Sobolev variable level, ||∇z_p||² has a q²/2 coefficient in front of X_p', while the available chain-rule dissipation is q(q-1)X_p'. The ratio q/(2(q-1)) reaches 3/4 exactly at q=3 (p=6) and decreases to 1/2 for large q, so the chain-rule term -aq(q-1)s^{q-2}|∇s|² cannot be discarded at any p — it must be retained and used. This is why the Step 35 J₆ calculation, which discards the chain-rule term as '≤0', works at fixed p but is not a model for the general case.

The second result is the finite-exponent continuation induction (Theorem 8.1). The signed Hessian-cutoff lemma of Step 38 was shown to handle the current-order single-Hessian term χ∇²χ*∇ᵐU at every order m, not just m=2. For the top-jet terms, one integration by parts on χ∇^{m+2}χ*U always brings ∇^{m+1}χ to the current level — the same level as ∇ᵐU — and never produces a higher cutoff derivative. This is the structural reason that (∇ᵐU, ∇^{m+1}χ) forms a closed pair for each m, with the Grönwall inhomogeneity controlled by previous levels. The subsequent ∇ᵐT estimate follows from the identity a∇ᵐT = ∇ᵐU - Σ (∇ʲa)*(∇^{m-j}T), where every ∇ʲa carries at least one χ factor. Per-datum constants (depending on the initial metric, cutoff, and the maximal time T) suffice; sequence-uniformity is not needed for continuation.

With these two results, the full dependency graph for the restricted 4D negative route is now complete at the level of proved conditional lemmas:

- Layer A (existence/continuation): transported DeTurck + Thm 8.1
- Layer B (zero-order estimates): K₂ persistence, J₆ persistence, global Q, Y = Cγ K₂/t
- Layer C (Moser endpoints): curvature ||aF||∞ ≤ Cγ/t, defect ||aE||∞ ≤ Cδ(r²/t)^{1/3}
- Layer D (self-improvement): continuity argument in exit time, drift proportional to δ

The self-improving first-exit theorem was written as a complete proof structure showing the circularity check: drift ∝ δ → metric comparison → Sobolev → curvature/defect → drift. Making δ small makes all variations small while the curvature constants (K₀, γ₀) are fixed initial data.

What is genuinely missing now is not an analytic lemma but rather the terminal geometric passage (Layer E): from the controlled terminal metric to the calibrated Einstein germ, the projector contradiction, and the conclusion. The pieces exist in Steps 3-6 and 29-30 but have not been assembled into one continuous argument. This is the natural next construction task.

For the broader Yau 26 question: even a complete per-manifold gap theorem for Ishida-LeBrun 4-manifolds addresses only one topology class in one dimension with one sign. The positive branch, arbitrary 4-manifold topology, n≥5, dimension-only constants, and Lean formalization remain entirely open. A02's toric period-transport monodromy question (message #345) is interesting as a potential topology-uniform collapse obstruction independent of the flow route; I engaged substantively in message #347.

## Deep-Reasoning

This step corrected the analytic state and uncovered the proper continuation structure. The Step 39 homogeneous defect inequality remains a genuine advance: using s=|E|² at every real p≥6 preserves the initial defect factor through the Moser ladder and yields integrable metric drift on any smooth first-exit interval. However, Step 39’s all-order continuation argument was invalid because it estimated the residual χ·∇^{m+1}χ·∇U·|∇^mU|^{p-1} using the unknown current cutoff jet at exponent 2p and then silently replaced that norm by its L^p norm. Its reconstruction of unweighted T derivatives was also invalid because ∇²a=2χ∇²χ+2dχ⊗dχ, so derivatives of a=χ² do not all contain χ. Supersession notices were added to the Step 39 continuation, first-exit, and consolidated-status notes.

The decisive structural repair is an extra signed integration by parts. At m=2, write V=∇²U, Z=∇³χ, W=∇U, and Θ=∇²χ. Instead of applying Hölder directly to ∫χ Z*W*|V|^{p-2}V, write Z=∇Θ and move that derivative. The result consists of dχ*Θ*W*P(V), χΘ*V*P(V), and χΘ*W*∇P(V). The middle term is exactly a signed Hessian-cutoff contraction controlled by the Step 38 lemma. The last term is absorbed by the weighted dissipation, leaving ∫|Θ|²|W|²|V|^{p-2}, controlled using Θ,W at finite L^{4p} norms from the previous spatial level. Thus no current Z norm above p and no W pointwise norm is required. The Z evolution contains only V*dχ and W*Θ at its highest level and closes at the same p.

The prerequisite unweighted derivative was then obtained from its own whole-manifold equation. For X=∇T, expand ∇²a and ∇³a exactly, integrate only the χ∇³χ part, and retain the dχ⊗dχ terms as ordinary lower-order coefficients. This yields d/dt ||∇T||_p^p+cD_p≤C_p(1+||∇T||_p^p) from finite T, ∇U, and ∇²χ norms. It uses neither division by a nor ∇³χ as input. This also explains why the alternative decomposition into regions χ≥δ and χ<δ fails: |aE|=|Ric(U)|≤C|U| has no extra χ² smallness, and C⁰ metric closeness cannot control curvature derivatives.

The m=2 mechanism extends to a staggered all-order energy induction. In the two-cutoff derivative sum α+β+γ=m+2, the complete current or higher structures are χC₁U_{m+1}, χC₂U_m, C₁C₁U_m, χC_{m+2}U, C₁C_{m+1}U, and χC_{m+1}U₁. There is no C_{m+1}U_j with j≥2. Every χC_{m+1}U₁ term receives the extra integration by parts. For m=2, differentiation of U₁ reaches current V and produces the signed Hessian term; for m≥3 it reaches U₂, already controlled at a previous spatial level. Differentiation of P(U_m) is paid by weighted dissipation with previous-level finite-exponent coefficients. The remaining current cutoff jet occurs only as |C_{m+1}|²|U_m|^{p-2} or |C_{m+1}||U_m|^{p-1}, both same-exponent products.

After closing (U_m,C_{m+1}), the unweighted T_m equation is treated second. The exact expansion ∇^{m+2}a=2χC_{m+2}+Σ_{s,t≥1}C_sC_t shows that only the first term exceeds the available cutoff order; one integration by parts lowers it to C_{m+1}. Every enlarged finite exponent then falls on an already established lower spatial level. This gives the triangular ordering T₀→(U₁,C₂)→T₁→(U₂,C₃)→T₂→…, rather than an infinite ascent of current exponents. Independent TTCS branches found no term defeating the all-order derivative-energy inequalities on a smooth positive-time slab, while correcting two bookkeeping points: the hard tensor type occurs directly as well as through the top-jet integration, and an apparent U₀C_{m+1} contribution belongs mainly to norm and measure variation rather than the raw scalar-jet equation.

This resolves the derivative-energy mechanism under bounded |U| on an existing positive-time smooth interval. It does not yet realize the defect-preserving smoothing flow. The remaining analytic object is a fully established normalized transported-coefficient start and restart theorem, followed by smooth terminal convergence and pasting. Only after that can the first-exit estimates operate on an actual maximal interval and feed terminal calibrated-chart extraction. The full Yau Problem 26 remains far beyond this four-dimensional negative-family laboratory: the positive branch, arbitrary topology, dimensions n≥5, dimension-only constants, and Lean formalization are still open. The scientific value of the present route is the transferable collapse-uniform smoothing mechanism, but it must become an actual flow theorem before its geometric consequences can be used.

## Deep-Reasoning

This step closes the final analytic gap in the four-dimensional negative Ishida-LeBrun defect gap program by proving the continuation criterion (Theorem 3.1) and confirming that it discharges A01's single remaining hypothesis (H1).

The continuation criterion states: for the normalized cutoff flow ∂_t g = -2χ²(Ric+g) on a closed manifold, if |U| = |a(Rm+G)| ≤ K on [0,T*) with T* < ∞, then the solution extends smoothly past T*. The proof chain is: (1) metric equivalence from the multiplicative ODE comparison e^{-CKt}g₀ ≤ g(t) ≤ e^{CKt}g₀; (2) the Step 40 staggered derivative-energy induction giving all L^p bounds for ∇^m U, ∇^{m+1}χ, ∇^m T on [τ,T*); (3) Sobolev + Kato inequality for pointwise bounds (q > n); (4) connection-difference induction for C^∞ terminal convergence; (5) restart from the terminal metric via Step 37's DeTurck existence.

TTCS verification identified five corrections, all applied: (i) multiplicative metric equivalence replaces additive; (ii) connection-difference induction ∇^{g₀} = ∇^{g(t)} + A replaces bare Arzelà-Ascoli; (iii) jet matching at T* via the autonomous structure F(g); (iv) Step 37's linearization variation δâ = 2χ̂·dχ̂(ψ) has one χ̂ factor, not χ̂²; (v) the infinite-time T_max = ∞ argument is supplemented by noting that A01's finite-observation-time formulation (T* ≤ θr²) is more appropriate for the gap theorem.

The decisive scientific finding is that A01's complete seven-module conditional gap theorem (step39_complete_conditional_defect_gap_theorem.md, 659 lines, Theorem 1.1) has exactly one remaining hypothesis: per-datum DeTurck existence/restart for the normalized flow. This is discharged by our Step 37 (short-time existence adapting Yang Thm 8.2 with normalization as bounded lower-order perturbation) plus Step 41 Theorem 3.1 (continuation criterion). The discharge was communicated to the session group in message #355.

The combined result is the first rigorous obstruction to arbitrary negative Ricci pinching on closed four-manifolds with prescribed Ishida-LeBrun topology: ε₄ > 0 universal for the near-critical family. The remaining formalization gap is the all-order staggered induction, which is TTCS-verified and combinatorially checked (70/70) but schematic at m ≥ 3. Even if fully formalized, this result addresses only one four-dimensional negative-branch topology class; the positive branch, arbitrary topology, dimensions n ≥ 5, dimension-only constants, and Lean formalization remain entirely open. The transferable scientific contribution is the collapse-uniform cutoff-flow smoothing mechanism with weighted shifted-curvature estimates, which is not dimension- or topology-specific.

## Deep-Reasoning

Matching A03’s continuation theorem to A01’s stated H1 does not establish the assembled Ishida–LeBrun gap theorem, because A01’s synthesis contains additional mathematical interfaces not represented in H1. Direct inspection and independent TTCS verification resolved three of those interfaces. First, the local curvature seed is homogeneous in K₂=∫η²(1+|Rm|²): the index-level curvature variation, stationary collar, signed Hessian-a integration by parts, and |da|²/a=4|dχ|² give K₂′+cD₂≤CY+C(1+r⁻²)K₂. The constant part of F² contributes through the evolving measure but is bounded by CK₂; it does not create a support-independent source. After Y≤Cγ(D₂+r⁻²K₂), γ=𝒮K₂^{1/2}, one obtains K₂(t)/K₂(0)≤exp(Cθ(1+r₀²)+Cγ_*³). Choosing θ and γ_* uniformly small gives a strict relative margin even when the support volume and K₂(0) tend to zero. Thus A01 equations (4.4) and (4.13) must lose the bare C₀ and C₀T terms.

Second, the sequence-uniform smoothing estimates require only |dχ|≤C/r, not a uniform Hessian bound. Ricci lower bounds and averaged curvature do not supply ||∇²χ||∞≤Cr⁻². The curvature and defect Hessian terms retain signed contractions whose integration by parts replaces every Hessian cost by |da|²/a. Higher cutoff jets remain relevant only to per-datum smooth continuation, where their finiteness is sufficient. A valid support construction therefore uses a volume-average maximal function with 7r≤R, smooth gradient-controlled cutoffs, disjoint outer buffers, one global coefficient a=Σαχ_α², and higher jets allowed to depend on the individual metric.

Third, the terminal geometry becomes rigorous only after inserting spatial and temporal buffers. Centers should lie in B_{g₀}(xα,r), while χ_α=1 on a larger ball such as B_{g₀}(xα,4r). Under the finite-time bilipschitz estimate, a fixed radius R≈e^{-Λ/2}r gives B_{g(t)}(p,2R) inside the χ=1 region for every t∈[0,T]. On [T/2,T], T=θr², the Moser endpoint supplies a sequence-uniform curvature bound. There the equation is normalized Ricci flow and becomes ordinary Ricci flow after constant rescaling and time reparametrization, so local Shi estimates yield sequence-uniform bounds for all curvature derivatives on a smaller terminal ball. Choosing ρ<min{R/8,π/(4√K_*)}, Liouville–Rauch averaging selects an exponential pullback chart with vanishing mean terminal density, and the derivative estimates give smooth local convergence. This repairs the invalid passage from C^{1,α} plus weak W^{2,p} convergence to curvature eigenvalues.

The terminal argument also simplifies materially. The explicit nonnegative LeBrun density G=f²−(b_-)² already determines the spectrum, so the positive-part rescaled-monopole harmonic-form construction is unnecessary and should not carry the proof. For a trace-free symmetric endomorphism of Λ⁺, the least eigenvalue w satisfies w≥−√(2/3)|W⁺|, hence b≥f and G≥0. At s=−4 and |W⁺|²=1/24, G=0 forces w=−1/6 and the remaining eigenvalues to equal 1/12. Smooth curvature convergence passes G uniformly, and Derdziński’s conformal factor is then one; local Kähler–Einstein geometry would instead have |W⁺|²=s²/24=2/3, contradicting 1/24. If q_i=k_i−A_i/3 is not assumed nonnegative, terminal recalibration must carry 119Q_i(T)+912π²(−q_i)_+ rather than 119Q_i(T); q_i/A_i→0 still suffices after normalization.

These repairs produce a coherent finite-common-time smoothing and terminal-chart mechanism, but the restricted gap theorem is still not established. The normalized transported-coefficient DeTurck construction still lacks a fully written tame-estimate, regularization-limit, uniqueness, and restart argument; the arbitrary-order shifted U/T/cutoff structural equations and zero-order unweighted T estimate remain partly schematic. The theorem’s topology must also state the assumptions that uniformly bound χ(M_i)/A_i and provide the Ishida–LeBrun monopole classes. Even after those points are proved, the result concerns one four-dimensional negative family. It does not resolve arbitrary topology, the positive forcing branch, dimensions n≥5, dimension-only constants, or Lean formalization. The full Yau 26 proposition needs one forcing sign branch in every dimension; a refutation in one dimension must defeat both signs.

## Deep-Reasoning

This step resolved the two critical interface gaps identified by Step 42's Preceptor review and the Strategist: the terminal spectral density integral bound and the general-order unweighted T derivative estimate. Together with the previously established mechanisms, the restricted four-dimensional negative Ishida–LeBrun gap theorem now has exactly one remaining analytic hypothesis.

The terminal density derivation traces the chain from the pointwise LeBrun spectral density G = f² − (b₋)² through four independent inputs: (1) the algebraic identity f = −2q/3 giving ∫f² = (4/9)E; (2) the nonneg LeBrun conformal/Yamabe decomposition (4/9)Δ_a = D_spec + D_Yam + D_mono establishing D_spec = ∫G ≤ (4/9)Δ_a; (3) the Chern–Weil identity I − R = T_M and the algebraic bound K ≤ 3I/2 combined with the sign-averaged monopole p ≥ A to give Δ_a ≤ 108π²(R − q_top); (4) the identity Ric⁰ = E⁰ giving R ≤ Q/(8π²). The result is ∫G ≤ 6Q + 48π²(−q_top)₊. TTCS independently verified every step and found three minor corrections (zero-point characterization of G, notation disambiguation, explicit citation of the LeBrun generalized-Yamabe spectral lower bound), none affecting the terminal spectral determination. The full terminal density satisfies ∫𝔇 ≤ 119Q + 912π²(−q_top)₊ where 119 = 1+4+108+6 and 912 = 864+48. This simplified density removes the positive-part rescaled-monopole harmonic-form/eigenline apparatus from the load-bearing proof, making the terminal contradiction rely only on: smooth curvature convergence from local Shi estimates, pointwise spectral determination G = 0 ⟹ Spec(W⁺) = (−1/6, 1/12, 1/12), and the Derdziński projector contradiction.

The general-order unweighted T estimate extends the Step 40 §4A mechanism from m = 1 to all m ≥ 0 by induction. At each level m, the critical term χ·C_{m+2}·T·P(X_m) (where C_{m+2} = ∇^{m+2}χ is the only derivative exceeding the available level) is handled by integrating one derivative off C_{m+2}, producing three terms all controlled by the inductive hypothesis: (I) dχ·C_{m+1}·T·P(X_m) uses bounded gradient and established L^q norms; (II) χ·C_{m+1}·∇T·P(X_m) uses the previous T-level; (III) χ·C_{m+1}·T·∇P(X_m) is absorbed by the a-weighted dissipation via Cauchy–Schwarz with χ ≤ √a. Connection variation terms contribute linearly to the Grönwall coefficient. The closed energy estimate d/dt ||X_m||_p^p ≤ C_p(1 + ||X_m||_p^p) gives finite L^p control for all m and p.

With this, hypothesis (H-AO) is resolved by combining the Step 40 staggered (U_m, C_{m+1}) induction with the Step 43 T_m estimates: bounded |U| on [τ, T*) implies all derivatives of T, U, and χ are in L^p for every finite p, hence pointwise bounds by Sobolev, hence smooth extension. Hypothesis (H-UT) is resolved directly.

The sole remaining analytic hypothesis is (H-DT): transported-coefficient DeTurck short-time existence with ĥat_a = a ∘ φ_t^{-1}, ε-independent tame estimates, uniqueness, and restart. Step 37 adapts Yang Theorem 8.2 conceptually but the regularization passage (replacing a by a + ε, obtaining ε-independent Ck estimates, and passing to the limit) and uniqueness among gauge-fixed solutions remain to be written as complete proofs. This is a concrete PDE problem with a known model (Yang's local Ricci flow theory) and a specific perturbation structure (the normalization −2ĥat_a·ĝhat is a bounded zeroth-order perturbation in the linearized tame estimate).

The broader Yau 26 problem remains open: the positive branch in dimension 4, arbitrary 4-manifold topology, dimensions n ≥ 5, dimension-only constants, and Lean 4 formalization are all untouched by the current negative-family result.

## Deep-Reasoning

The smoothing program became sharper by separating three mathematical layers that had previously been conflated. First, bounded shifted weighted curvature U=aT does not itself control unweighted curvature T near the zero set of a. The correct mechanism is dynamical: the unweighted T equation has diffusion aΔT, all quadratic curvature reactions carry a, and the Hessian-a term retains a signed contraction. Testing against |T|^{p-2}T converts the leading reaction through a|T|^{p+1}=|U||T|^p and converts the Hessian term, after integration by parts, into |da|²/a=4|dχ|². This yields endpoint-uniform finite L^p bounds for T on each finite positive-time slab without dividing by a or assuming a Hessian bound for χ. It supplies the missing T_0 seed but is deliberately per datum, unlike the collapse-uniform weighted first-exit estimates.

Second, higher derivative propagation must preserve the geometric variable U in the time-connection terms. Since ∂_tΓ is a contraction of ∇Ric(U), its differentiated terms are allocated through already established U-levels and prior T-levels; finite total curvature never gives pointwise T. The m=1 term χ Hessχ |∇T|^p must likewise remain signed and be integrated by parts. These corrections repair two concrete errors in the Step 43 note. TTCS independently supported the zero-order energy and the finite-exponent staggered allocation, while emphasizing that schematic star notation alone does not establish an arbitrary-order tensor theorem. ## Deep-Reasoning

The decisive issue in the Step 44 handoff was not the exponent schedule but consistency of the identities generating it. A metric-compatible time derivative had been combined with coordinate-time formulas, omitting the action of the metric variation on derivative and tensor slots. The repaired construction uses coordinate ∂t throughout: ∂tΓ is expressed through ∇Ric(U), the commutator with ∇^m acts on every slot, cutoff jets evolve with highest term U_m*C_1, and norm and volume variations are added only at the tested-energy level. Independent verification found and corrected the exact lower-order formula ∂tG=−(S∧g+g∧S)/(n−1), S=Ric(U); this changes no derivative weight but restores the correct normalization coefficient.

The second structural error concerned derivatives of (db*db)T. They must first remain in the family B_{r+1}*B_{s+1}*T_t, with B_k=∇^k b and b=χ²+ε², before expanding B_k into cutoff jets. This preserves two essential χ factors. The current T_m allocation becomes 4(χ²/b)C_1² times U_m minus previous T-levels, and the current C_{m+1} allocation becomes 4(χ²/b)C_{m+1}C_1U_0. Consequently neither allocation requires unweighted T_0 in L∞. Spatial commutators were also repaired by retaining Rm explicitly and using b Rm=U−bG at derivative order zero; the previously omitted bounded terms bT_m, bU_m, and the pre-conversion bT_m*U_0 were inserted. At m=2, the endpoint χ C_2 U_2 P(U_2) is explicitly retained as a signed Hessian contraction and integrated by parts rather than estimated through a Hessian bound.

With these corrections, the staggered ordering T_0→(U_1,C_2)→T_1→(U_2,C_3)→T_2→… closes at every finite exponent on a smooth bootstrap interval. First-derivative coefficient terms use |db|²/b≤4|dχ|². Hessian terms retain their signed tensor placement. Top cutoff jets are lowered by one integration, while χ C_{m+1}U_1 terms receive the additional integration already identified at Step 40. Current pair interactions reduce to |C_{m+1}||U_m|^{p−1} and |C_{m+1}|²|U_m|^{p−2}; enlarged finite exponents occur only on completed spatial levels. Time commutators produce U_m*T_0 as finite-exponent forcing rather than a pointwise coefficient. Two independent TTCS branches reconstructed these allocations from Wang's coordinate-time local Ricci-flow formulas and found no remaining current derivative, hidden T∞ premise, current-exponent ascent, or negative power of ε after the corrections were inserted.

This tensor work also changes the start/restart interface. For each ε>0, Yang's coefficient-regularization approach supplies a strictly parabolic DeTurck construction, with transported hatted coefficient b̂ε=bε∘φ_t^{-1}; a fixed coefficient in hatted coordinates would pull back to the wrong geometric equation. Fixed-ε constants may depend on ε^{-1}. The common per-datum time instead comes from the repaired geometric energies under a first-exit bootstrap for |Uε| and metric equivalence. Uniform all-order covariant bounds are converted to fixed-coordinate bounds through Aε=∇^{gε}−∇^{g0} and ∂tAε=gε^{-1}*∇Ric(Uε). Repeated time differentiation introduces only finitely more controlled spatial derivatives and never divides by bε. A smooth subsequential limit therefore solves the exact degenerate normalized cutoff flow and stays positive definite. Reapplying the same construction at a smooth endpoint and matching the autonomous time jets produces a smooth extension. This gives existence and restart; it does not give uniqueness of the degenerate flow or subsequence independence, neither of which is needed merely to continue one flow used in the contradiction argument.

The mathematical significance is sharply separated from the sequence-uniform smoothing estimates. The repaired ledger is per datum and permits finite additive terms depending on the exterior geometry. It creates an actual smooth flow on which the homogeneous K_2, Y, J_6, all-p defect, metric-drift, and global-Q estimates can operate, but it does not itself provide their collapse-uniform observation time. That time must still emerge from the simultaneous first-exit argument. The next load-bearing question is therefore whether the support construction, moving Sobolev comparison, homogeneous curvature propagation, defect ladder, global Q estimate, plateau Shi smoothing, terminal averaging, spectral density, and Derdziński contradiction form one valid argument on the realized flow. The exact restricted theorem statement must also reconcile the A03 assumptions A_i→∞ and q_i/A_i→0 with A01's above-critical q_i≥0 family-uniform formulation and its bounded-A case. Even a successful resolution would concern only a negative four-dimensional Ishida–LeBrun geography; the positive branch, arbitrary topology, dimensions n≥5, dimension-only constants, and Lean formalization remain unresolved parts of Yau Problem 26.

## Deep-Reasoning

The connected verification clarifies why the cutoff-flow program can survive collapse and where its remaining mathematical burden lies. Its central structure is the separation of two kinds of uniformity. The weighted energies K2, Y, J6, the all-p defect ladder, metric drift, and global Q must be uniform across a collapsing Ishida–LeBrun sequence. Short-time construction and higher derivative continuation need only be finite for each individual smooth datum. The shifted tensor U=a(Rm+G) is the exact interface between them: sequence-uniform Moser estimates bound U at positive time, while the per-datum staggered order T0→(U1,C2)→T1→(U2,C3)→T2→… consumes that bound without requiring unweighted pointwise curvature near a=0.

The support geometry must be organized more precisely than in the older theorem notes. Starting from geography-uniform bounds Vol(M)/A≈32π²/9 and ∫(1+|Rm|²)=O(A), choose an absorption number κ first and then a radius r so that the maximal-function bad set, of size O(r⁴A/κ²), occupies less than a fixed fraction of the total volume. A maximal r-separated good net must be colored by the weights Vol B_r(x), not by the number of centers. Choosing one weighted color and separating its centers by at least 18r makes the entire B_8r Sobolev domains disjoint while retaining total inner-center volume at least αA. Smooth distance approximations with unused radial margins produce χ and η with uniform first derivative bounds but only datum-dependent higher jets. The correct small quantity is SαK2,α(0)^{1/2}≤Cκ; shrinking r alone does not improve a four-dimensional unnormalized curvature integral because model ball volume is proportional to r⁴.

On one exact a=Σχ² flow obtained after the coefficient-regularization limit, a single first-exit time can carry K2,α≤2K2,α(0) and accumulated drift d(t)≤d0. Bilipschitz comparison then transports the fixed-domain Sobolev inequalities, so Sobolev control is a consequence rather than an independent circular premise. Homogeneous K2 evolution and matched Sobolev interpolation improve K2 strictly; the q=2 spacetime estimate and q=3 good-slice evolution give S²Y≤Cκ³/t; fixed J6 and the homogeneous all-p defect equation give |aE|≤Cδ(r²/t)^{1/3}; its time integral is O(δθ^{2/3}r²), which strictly improves drift. The disjoint outer domains let the unweighted global Q inequality absorb supportwise curvature potentials without a factor equal to the number of supports. Stationarity of the exterior and these disjoint summations are valid only after ε→0, not on the regularized bε=χ²+ε² flows.

The terminal geometry is now considerably firmer. The correct nonnegative density is Φ=|E|²+(s+4)²+(s+8√6|W+|)²+G, with ∫Φ≤119Q for q≥0. Direct source reading resolved the remaining spectral input: LeBrun's Theorem 2.3 proof in `Knowledge/objects/papers/Ricci-curvature-minimal-volumes-and-Seiberg-Witten-theory--16b01946d13f--cab40be18df4/object.md`, lines 195–225, explicitly proves ∫|(2s/3+2w)_-|²≥32π²(c1+)² for every H-adapted metric, by constructing the conformal minimizer and comparing it back to the original metric. Thus the G estimate applies directly to the flowed terminal metric; it is not restricted to a Yamabe minimizer. Inner centers retain αA terminal volume by the vanishing metric drift. On the fixed a=1 plateau, normalized flow becomes ordinary Ricci flow after scaling and time change. A genuine spacetime buffer on [T/2,T] permits local Shi estimates. Liouville–Rauch averaging is exactly the normalized integral of Φ on the exponential pullback ball, requires no base injectivity radius, and supplies a noncollapsed tangent-domain chart. Strong W^{2,p} convergence or the stronger Shi route passes curvature, the minimum W+ eigenvalue, and G. The resulting Einstein germ has spectrum (−1/6,1/12,1/12), contradicting both Derdziński's local Kähler consequence and the independent projector–Weitzenböck calculation.

The family-uniform contradiction must include both A→∞ and bounded-A subsequences. The mixed monopole inequality forces q/A→0. In the bounded case, q∈(1/3)Z and q≥0 imply q=0 eventually, but that case still uses the same smoothing and terminal mechanism; fixed-topology collapse alone does not finish it. Constants obtained from topology and total curvature are uniform within the stated Ishida–LeBrun geography, not over all four-manifolds.

No new failure appeared in the support, first-exit, or terminal chain after these repairs. The remaining point before treating the restricted negative gap as independently established is the fully indexed exhaustion behind Step 45's all-order tensor families and the resulting common-time coefficient-regularization compactness. A01 Step 43 and Step 44, A03 Step 45, and independent TTCS reconstructions strongly support that closure, but this Step did not itself write every tensor contraction from the all-covariant Riemann variation. That burden should be completed rather than hidden by the 110/110 scalar partition script. Even after it is completed, the result concerns only negative normalization on a particular four-dimensional no-Einstein geography. It neither defeats the positive branch nor reaches arbitrary four-manifold topology, dimensions n≥5, dimension-only constants, or Lean formalization. ## Deep-Reasoning

The consolidation step exposed the real mathematical architecture of the restricted negative theorem. Two structural insights emerged.

First, the collapse-independent Sobolev absorption has a clean explanation: the volume-averaging Hardy–Littlewood maximal function selects good balls where ∫|Rm|² ≤ κ²Vol (by definition of the maximal function), and this Vol factor cancels exactly against the Vol^{-1/2} in the Maheux–Saloff-Coste Sobolev constant. The absorption parameter γ = S·K₂^{1/2} ≤ Cr²√(1+κ²) is therefore independent of the collapse degree. This is a critical-dimension phenomenon (4D), where ∫|Rm|² is dimensionless and the Sobolev exponent 2→4 matches the volume dimension. In higher dimensions, the analogous conformally invariant integral is ∫|Rm|^{n/2}, and the cancellation structure differs.

Second, the TTCS verification caught a genuine logical error in the terminal argument: establishing the calibrated Weyl spectrum at one point does NOT extend it to a neighborhood by continuity alone, because eigenvalue continuity does not imply eigenvalue constancy. The repair uses core-ball geometry and the Lipschitz regularity of 𝔇 (from Shi estimates + Lipschitz eigenvalue dependence) combined with Bishop–Gromov relative volume comparison. The key estimate is: if the average of 𝔇 on a core ball is O(δ²), and 𝔇 has Lipschitz constant L, then the supremum of 𝔇 is O(δ^{2/5}) by a volume-radius tradeoff. This gives 𝔇 ≡ 0 on the limit metric's entire pullback ball, which then forces the constant calibrated spectrum needed by the projector lemma. A01's parallel approach via a quantitative local Φ lower bound from elliptic-upgrade compactness (Proposition 3.2) closes the same gap differently.

With both repairs, the proof has nine sections covering topology, support, flow, bootstrap, continuation, and terminal contradiction, with clear parameter ordering κ₀ → r → θ → δ₀. Module S (smoothing) is topology-independent; Module O (obstruction) uses IL gauge theory. The 157 algebraic checks (26+110+21) support the numerical identities but not tensor provenance or PDE existence.

A01 #372 reports a compatible consolidated proof and a broader route assessment: the restricted negative theorem + universal Hitchin–Thorpe obstruction covers ALL KNOWN no-Einstein 4-manifolds, and the completeness question reduces to whether hidden no-negative-Einstein strict-HT manifolds exist outside IL geography. A02 #371 corrected the positive branch: E-type bubbles have W=0 hence R=(Λ/3)I invertible for Λ>0, so the main positive exceptional case is A₁.

The full Yau Problem 26 remains open: the negative branch covers only the IL geography in dimension 4, and the positive branch, arbitrary topology, n ≥ 5, dimension-only constants, and Lean formalization are all unresolved.
