## Deep-Reasoning

The full Yau 26 problem remains unresolved: no dimension-only interval has been proved, no fixed dimension has been shown to defeat both normalized signs, and no complete Lean formalization exists. This Step repaired two scope errors that had begun to redirect the session group, then converted the negative graph-neck route from an incorrectly closed route into a sharply localized construction problem.

For the diagonal orthogonally transitive metric g=e^{2phi}(dt^2+dz^2)+e^{2b}dx^2+e^{2c}dy^2, the exact anisotropy equation div(e^sigma grad d)=0, with d=b-c and sigma=b+c, still gives valid finite-cylinder rigidity. But for E=Ric+3g the equation is div(e^sigma grad d)=-e^{sigma+2phi}(E_x-E_y). Step 72 had neither a geometry-uniform inverse estimate for this sourced operator nor an upper bound on collar length. The normal balance only supplied a lower length scale under particular endpoint data. Consequently, the former O(delta log(1/delta)) forcing assertion and the resulting exclusion of approximate T^2 necks were withdrawn. The equations themselves describe only the diagonal orthogonally transitive subclass, not every T^2-invariant metric.

The decisive constructive test is the expanding tail
 g=dr^2+e^{2r}[dz^2+N^{-2}e^v dx^2+N^{-2}e^{-v}dy^2].
Writing B=dr^2+e^{2r}dz^2 and L v=v_{rr}+3v_r+e^{-2r}v_{zz}, direct substitution into all five Ricci components gives E|_B=-(1/2)dv tensor dv, E_x=-(1/2)Lv, E_y=(1/2)Lv, with base-fiber mixed components zero while the base rz component is generally nonzero. Hence the exact pointwise operator norm is (1/2)max{v_r^2+e^{-2r}v_z^2, |Lv|}. For v=chi((r-r0)/K)v0(z), this yields ||E||_infinity <= C(K^{-1}+K^{-2}+e^{-2r0}), uniformly in the lattice parameter N. The symbolic computation in workspace/scripts/step73_expanding_tail_verify.py reduced every formula residual to zero. Its data file workspace/data/step73_expanding_tail.json records, for v0=sin z and r0=6, grid maxima 0.7406712, 0.3563953, 0.1763899, 0.08796675, and 0.04395483 for K=4,8,16,32,64. Analytically K||E|| tends to 45/16=2.8125 for the chosen smootherstep. Thus an order-one orbit-ratio oscillation can be removed with arbitrarily small full Ricci defect once the geometry has entered a sufficiently long expanding region.

This tail also clarifies the normal equation rather than evading it. Its shape operator is diag(1,1+v_r/2,1-v_r/2), so H=3, |S-I|^2=v_r^2/2, and E_rr=-v_r^2/2. The negative normal residual exactly pays the tail's own shear pointwise. It does not pay the earlier deficit accumulated in moving from a reflection center with H=0 to an almost-cusp entry slice.

The special calculation extends to a general adiabatic tail. For h_r=e^{2a(r)}q_s, s=(r-r0)/K, and Q=q_s^{-1} dot q_s, the Gaussian formulas give S=a'I+Q/(2K), H=3a'+tr(Q)/(2K), explicit rr and tangential defect formulas, and E_{r dot}=(div Q-d tr Q)/(2K), whose g-norm contains e^{-a}. Under uniform positive definiteness and bounds on q_s, its inverse, parameter derivatives, Ric(q_s), and the Codazzi term, choosing a'=1-epsilon eta(s) gives ||Ric+3g||_infinity <= C(epsilon+K^{-1}+K^{-2}+e^{-2a0}). If q_s is stationary near both endpoints and q_1 is flat, the outgoing end is an exact flat hyperbolic cusp germ. TTCS independently verified these formulas and corrected important details: volume preservation improves only the normal path term, while the full defect generally remains O(K^{-1}); a smooth attachment requires endpoint-neighborhood constancy and agreement of all jets; and the mixed Codazzi term requires spatial derivative control.

This creates a precise core-entry interface. A core must reach a large slice h=e^{2a}q with S=(1-epsilon)I+P, epsilon and P small, e^{-2a}|Ric(q)| small, and enough jet control to begin a bounded path from q to the desired flat cusp metric. Merely having P tend to zero is insufficient: in the tail parametrization the initial path must realize Q(0)=2KP, and Q/K, (dot Q+Q^2)/K^2, the scaled Codazzi term, and higher jets must remain small. In the stronger exactly umbilic case the matching is simpler.

In a CMC, pointwise-volume-preserving foliation gauge, which is an additional structural assumption, an exact core satisfies a''=1-(a')^2-|P|^2/3, P'+3a'P=e^{-2a}Ric(q)^circ, e^{-2a}R(q)+6(1-(a')^2)+|P|^2=0, and div_q P=0. At a reflection center a'=0, P=0, and R(q)=-6e^{2a}. These equations expose the real mechanism: once expansion and scaled intrinsic curvature control have both been achieved, the traceless shape is damped and the tail can finish the construction. Expansion alone does not control e^{-2a}|Ric(q)|, and the elliptic Cauchy nature leaves growing spatial modes. Source study found that Witten-Yau/Cai-Galloway excludes the flat or other nonnegative-Yamabe two-ended Poincare-Einstein version, but not negative-Yamabe conformal infinity; no retrieved theorem supplied or excluded the required reflection-symmetric R x T^3 core.

The Step also preserved the distinction between the elliptic principal subsystem and the full Einstein equations. The determinant 2(tau^2+xi^2)^3 for (E_tt+E_zz,E_x,E_y) is useful, but these three equations do not force E_tt-E_zz and E_tz to vanish. Future construction must solve a full Einstein-DeTurck problem and eliminate the DeTurck field, or prove propagation of the Hamilton and momentum components from compatible data. Numerical convergence of only the three elliptic equations would repeat the earlier incomplete BVP.

The second group correction concerns products. A particular four-dimensional near-positive-Einstein input can be multiplied by a positively Einstein sphere to produce higher-dimensional near-pinched input families. This does not prove P_4^+ implies P_n^+ for arbitrary n-manifolds, and absence of arbitrary Einstein metrics does not pass automatically to products because an output Einstein metric need not split. Group message #512 circulated both corrections; A02 and A01 acknowledged them in messages #513, #515, and #519. Supersession notices were inserted into the Step 72 note, status, and route map.

A01's concurrent positive mixed-row work reports that the relative product deformation on (S^2 x S^2)/Z_2 has Einstein-operator eigenvalue -Lambda rather than zero, so the Ozuch infinitesimal Einstein space is reported to vanish; first obstructions vanish for Eguchi-Hanson directions in the two-dimensional kernel of R^plus or R^minus, and one second-order component vanishes by the rank-one curvature structure. This is promising but not yet an existence theorem. The remaining second components still require source-level verification, and Ozuch explicitly describes an infinite sequence of higher obstructions. Moreover, Ozuch Question 0.8 and Conjecture 2.22 are stated for Ricci-flat degeneration, whereas this product quotient has positive Einstein constant. Thus these results cannot yet be used as a sufficient positive desingularization theorem.

The main conceptual advance is therefore a decomposition of the negative construction into a solved long-tail module and an unsolved core-entry module. Exact anisotropy propagation is not the decisive obstruction; reaching a large, almost umbilic, scaled-curvature-controlled slice while satisfying all Einstein components is. This is substantially narrower and more constructive than the previous formulation. Success would combine naturally with graph four-manifolds already known to exclude every Einstein metric, but it would address only the normalized negative branch in dimension four. The positive branch, other dimensions, the complete quantifiers, and formalization remain open.

## Deep-Reasoning

This step developed the core-entry problem for the graph-manifold negative branch of Yau 26, producing three structural results and one important correction.

The z-independent impossibility is the cleanest new result. For g = dt² + e^{2a(t)}dz² + e^{2b(t)}dx² + e^{2c(t)}dy², the fiber slices are flat T³ with zero intrinsic curvature. The Gauss equations give H' + H² = 9 (tangential sum) and H' + |S|² = 3 (normal), so |S|² = H² − 6. At the reflection center H = 0, |S|² = 0, this yields −6 = 0, an algebraic contradiction. The approximate version gives δ ≥ 3/2, matching the Step 63 collar barrier. The related isotropic impossibility shows that S = sI on T³ forces Ric(q₀) = −2g₀, which in three dimensions means constant sectional curvature −2/3, excluded by Preissmann since π₁(T³) is abelian. Together these prove that z-dependence and anisotropy are both structurally necessary: no shortcut through ODEs or isotropic models exists.

The more important finding is the general constraint |S|² = H² − 6 − R₃(q_t), which gives R₃(q₀) = −6 at the center. This is the Koiso condition. The intrinsic curvature of the z-dependent fiber resolves the impossibility: a scalar-curvature −6 metric on T³ exists in the negative-Yamabe class through the conformal equation −8u″ − 2(f′)²u = −6u⁵, verified numerically for f = sin z. The traceless Ricci Ric(q₀)° is nonzero and drives the initial anisotropy P′(0) = e^{−2a(0)}Ric(q₀)°.

The linearized mode analysis around the flat cusp g₀ = dt² + e^{2t}(dz² + dx² + dy²) decomposes the T²-invariant Einstein system into: (i) the trace h = α + β + γ satisfying h″ + 2h′ = 0, decaying at rate 2; (ii) the sum w = β + γ constrained to be constant in t for k ≠ 0 by E₀z = 0; (iii) the anisotropy ψ = β − γ satisfying ψ″ + 3ψ′ − k²e^{−2t}ψ = 0; and (iv) a coupling relation 4D + k²W = 0 from E_zz. The anisotropy equation reduces to a modified Bessel equation with ν = 3/2 under x = ke^{−t} and ψ = x^{3/2}z. TTCS caught a chain-rule sign error in my initial derivation: the correct variable-change equation is x²ψ_xx − 2xψ_x − x²ψ = 0, not x²ψ_xx + 4xψ_x − x²ψ = 0, and the correct substitution is ψ = x^{3/2}z, not x^{−3/2}z. This changes the asymptotics completely: both branches ψ = x^{3/2}I_{3/2}(x) and ψ = x^{3/2}K_{3/2}(x) are bounded as t → ∞, with the I-branch decaying as e^{−3t} and the K-branch approaching √(π/2) ≈ 1.253. There are no exponentially growing modes. The corrected Bessel solutions match direct ODE integration to 10^{−12} precision.

The BVP structure is: since both branches are bounded, Neumann + boundedness alone does not determine a unique solution (only one constraint for a second-order ODE). The correct formulation is Neumann at the center plus Dirichlet at the far end, which is unique by the energy identity (e^{3t}ψ′)′ − k²e^tψ = 0. The k = 0 mode has a free constant (cusp cross-section shape modulus) that must be fixed by the global geometry. The TTCS verification also confirmed that full constraint propagation requires all five Einstein equations, not just the anisotropy difference.

The CMC gauge ODE model (a simplified version with scalar coupling) shows the core naturally reaches near-cusp data (|S − I|² < 0.01) by t ≈ 3, making the nonlinear core a compact BVP on [0, R] × S¹ with R ≈ 5. This is a standard domain for numerical elliptic PDE solvers.

The overall picture for the negative branch is now sharply decomposed: the tail is solved, the linearized modes are favorable (no amplification), and the nonlinear core BVP on a compact domain is the critical bottleneck. The positive branch (Ozuch desingularization) has been substantially corrected by A01 and A02: the scalar kernel modes must be properly sliced, the inter-node Green response uses the full product P-resolvent with additive spectral denominators, and the Bianchi-corrected local scalar projection vanishes. Both branches have well-defined mathematical next steps, but the graph-manifold negative branch is closer to producing a concrete result.

## Deep-Reasoning

The full Yau 26 problem remains unresolved: no dimension-only pinching interval has been proved, no fixed dimension has been shown to defeat both normalized signs, and no Lean formalization of a final mathematical resolution exists. This Step nevertheless changed the negative graph-neck program substantially by replacing an unsupported fixed-length nonlinear core picture with two exact structures: unavoidable contraction at a reflected torus center and compulsory anisotropy flux at every viable finite exit.

The Step 74 mode equation was correct, but its interpretation was not. For ψ''+3ψ'−k²e^(−2t)ψ=0, the two standard radial basis functions are bounded in t for each fixed k, yet the solution normalized by ψ(0)=1 and ψ'(0)=0 satisfies lim ψ=sinh(k)/k. The transfer factors 1.175, 1.813, 3.339, 14.841, and 186.310 for k=1,2,3,5,8 show exponential frequency amplification. Fixed-mode Neumann–Dirichlet uniqueness therefore supplies neither frequency-uniform control nor invertibility of the nonlinear Einstein map. The prescribed CMC ordinary differential model also did not evolve its curvature source from an intrinsic metric satisfying the Hamilton and momentum equations. Moreover, the normal identity e^(2R)(3−H(R))=3+∫e^(2r)(|S−I|²+E_rr)dr shows that physical Gaussian length must diverge when both the full defect and 3−H(R) vanish. These facts remove the former premise that a core interval of length about five is geometrically sufficient.

A new exact theorem identifies the local burden at every T²-cohomogeneity-one reflected center. For q=ds²+G(s) on T³, with flat T² orbits, A=(1/2)G^(−1)G' and h=tr A, one has R_q=−2h'−|A|²−h². Since h=(log sqrt(det G))' is periodic with mean zero, either h is identically zero or it has a downward zero. At such a zero, if R_q=−6, then the orbit-plane sectional curvature is K_orb=−det A=|A|²/2=3−h'≥3. The orbit-normal direction is an eigenvector of Ric_q+3I with eigenvalue −K_orb≤−3. At an exact reflected four-dimensional Einstein center, S'(0)=Ric_q+3I, so some principal direction initially contracts with acceleration at most −3. This is not peculiar to the sinusoidal seed and includes non-diagonal periodic 2×2 orbit metrics.

The small-defect version was strengthened by independent verification after the main note was written. If E=Ric_4+3g and ||E||_op≤δ, then e=R_q+6=tr_T E−E_nn. Combining the downward-zero equation directly with S'=Ric_q+3I−E_T avoids counting E_vv twice and gives λ_min S'(0)≤−3+3δ. The workspace note and symbolic JSON currently contain the weaker valid constant −3+5δ and must be amended; group messages #537–#538 also stopped at the weaker constant. The exact equivalence is between K_orb≥3 and the selected orbit-normal eigenvalue being at most −3, not between K_orb≥3 and the existence of an unspecified small eigenvalue.

The anisotropy equation supplies the complementary outer-face structure. In conformal coordinates for the diagonal orthogonally-transitive class, d=b−c satisfies div(e^(b+c) grad d)=0 for an exact Einstein metric. Reflection makes its normal derivative zero at the inner face. If the two orbit principal curvatures are also equal at a finite outer face, the weighted energy identity forces d to be constant everywhere. The center metric is then conformal to a flat torus metric, which cannot have scalar curvature −6 by the integrated Yamabe equation. Thus a successful finite interface cannot become exactly umbilic in the orbit directions. It must retain nonzero d_n at every finite stage, even if its unweighted size tends to zero; exponential geometric weights may allow that small derivative to carry a nonvanishing flux into the Step 73 adiabatic tail.

The center theorem explains the center-shape computations. In the reciprocal-warp Yamabe family, the sampled maximum positive sectional curvature fell from 5.323 at amplitude one to 3.126 at amplitude eight, 3.090 at amplitude ten, and 3.051 at amplitude fifteen. A three-mode shape search reached 3.03297. The analytic theorem proves the value three is a lower bound throughout the whole T²-cohomogeneity-one center class, so these high-amplitude seeds approach the sharp local obstruction rather than eliminating initial shear. Attempts to search a broader independent two-warp family timed out because each shape evaluation solved a nonlinear periodic Yamabe problem; their incomplete console samples did not produce a durable result and are not used.

Several full-five-component Gaussian searches were then used to pressure the corrected formulation. Runs that fixed equal orbit derivatives at the outer face were recognized as solving an already impossible exact problem. The most relevant free-flux run fixed the Fourier-projected Step 69 center and its projected Koiso second jet, left the outer metric and anisotropy flux free, and minimized E_rr, E_rz, E_zz, E_x, and E_y together. Its sampled operator suprema remained approximately 16.03, 16.03, and 15.96 for R=2,4,6, concentrated near physical radius 0.19. A continuation from a numerical germ at t=0.15 similarly retained sampled suprema 23.52, 22.12, and 21.60 near the inner interface. Independent reading confirmed the Ricci formulas and orthonormal normalization, but also found that all iterations ended at the function-evaluation cap, optimized an averaged Frobenius residual rather than the operator supremum, lacked off-grid testing, and used only a Fourier projection of the continuous center. The germ continuation matched only metric and first normal derivative, while its global radial basis coupled outer value and derivative. These computations therefore establish only that the tested finite spectral parameterizations did not resolve the analytic jet cascade; they do not supply a numerical lower bound or geometric nonexistence result.

The negative construction problem is now more precise. A parameter-dependent core must transform an order-three initial contraction into an outer state with small full Einstein defect, small S−I, small scaled intrinsic curvature, and a small but nonzero anisotropy derivative carrying the required weighted flux. Exact finite umbilicity is impossible, while the Step 73 long tail shows that approximate flattening after such an entry is inexpensive. The decisive mathematical question is whether the center contraction, anisotropy flux, and normal weighted balance combine into a global positive cost, or whether a multiscale core can redistribute them over increasing physical length. Either answer would materially advance the negative branch. Even success there would leave the positive branch and the all-dimensional quantifiers; peer messages #535–#539 also show that the current positive-orbifold local obstruction calculations remain nondecisive for the original problem.

## Deep-Reasoning

The full Yau 26 statement remains unresolved: there is still no dimension-only pinching interval, no fixed-dimensional family defeating both normalized signs while excluding every Einstein metric, and no Lean formalization of a final resolution. This Step nevertheless changed the negative graph-neck route at its load-bearing point. The Step 75 center theorem does not by itself impose a positive Ricci-defect cost. It identifies order-one anisotropy energy that must be transported, while the expanding geometry supplies a concrete way for its local density and unweighted derivative to decay.

For q=ds²+G(s) with ρ=√det G, h=ρ′/ρ, A=G⁻¹G′/2, and A₀=A−hI/2, periodicity and Rq=−6+e give the exact integrated identity ∫ρ|A₀|²=6∫ρ+(1/2)∫ρh²−∫ρe. In the diagonal case d=b−c this becomes ∫ρd_s²=12∫ρ+∫ρh²−2∫ρe. Hence an exact scalar-minus-six center has normalized energy ⟨d_s²⟩ρ≥12, and a reflected four-dimensional core with ‖Ric+3g‖op≤δ has ⟨d_s²⟩ρ≥12−8δ. Lattice quotients multiply energy and volume equally, so collapse in the two orbit directions cannot remove this normalized center burden. This integrated result is more informative than minimizing the largest positive sectional curvature at one orbit.

The correct transport quantity is subtler than the earlier wording suggested. For divγ(ρ∇d)=−ρX, X=E_x−E_y, an exact reflected core has conserved total signed flux Q=∫ρd_n=0. Its Dirichlet energy is carried instead by the covariance F_c=∫(d−c)ρd_n: exactly, F_c(R)=∫coreρ|∇d|². Thus a nonconstant exact core cannot have d_n identically zero at a finite exit, but it need not have nonzero net flux. With forcing, F_c acquires the bulk term −∫(d−c)ρX, so even identically zero exit derivative is not excluded without geometric control of d−c. The slice law F_c′=∫ρ[d_r²+|∇slice d|²−(d−c)X] shows that the center energy gives F_c′(0)≥12 Vol(q₀), but Ricci pinching alone gives no uniform physical thickness over which that slope persists.

The expanding Fourier model makes the escape mechanism explicit. The reflection-normalized solution of ψ″+3ψ′−k²e^(−2t)ψ=0 satisfies ψ(∞)=sinh(k)/k and ψ′(t)∼k sinh(k)e^(−2t). Hence unweighted shear tends to zero while e^(2t)ψ′ approaches a finite weighted stress. Total covariance can grow with the expanding slice volume while covariance per unit volume decays like sinh²(k)e^(−2t). This does not produce an exact Einstein core—the remaining base defect is −(1/2)dd⊗dd—but it proves that the center energy floor alone cannot yield a uniform residual lower bound. It also isolates a genuine high-frequency issue: a parameter family needs A_j e^(−R_j)sinh(k_j)→0 or comparable analytic regularity.

The CMC volume-gauge equation gives the tensor version of the same mechanism. For g=dr²+e^(2a)q_r, q_r′=2q_rP, tr P=0, exact Einstein evolution satisfies (e^(3a)P)′=e^a Ric(q_r)^∘. If a(r)=r+O(1) and the intrinsic traceless Ricci tensor remains controlled, then P(R)=O(e^(−2R)); the finite output is e^(2a)P or the covariance pairing, not P itself. A successful obstruction would have to separate the weighted stress produced by reflected scalar-minus-six centers from the weighted stress admitted by negative-Yamabe PE ends. The current identities do not provide such a separation.

Reading the Li–Liu source sharpened this into a source-grounded scattering problem. Their Type-I Toda equation constructs exact Ric=−3 metrics on (0,∞)×T³ with one PE end and one AH cusp end for arbitrary T² boundary data, but no horizontal level is totally geodesic. Nonnegative-Yamabe one-endedness does not apply to their nonflat negative-Yamabe conformal infinities. More importantly, their conformal-boundary geometry activates an off-diagonal orbit direction omitted by the diagonal core searches. In a local one-variable gauge q=e^φ(dz²+dx²)+(dy+A dx)², the Toda Dirichlet-to-Neumann datum p=v_ξ(0,z) obeys A_z=(1/2)e^φp, and direct curvature computation gives Rq=−e^(−φ)φ_zz−p²/8. Therefore Rq=−6 implies ∫e^φp²=48∫e^φ. The BVP1 conserved average also gives ∫e^φp=0, so any intersection has weighted mean zero and weighted variance 48: it is necessarily finite-amplitude and cannot arise perturbatively from flat data. The associated unimodular orbit matrix lies in SL(2,R)/SO(2), showing that scalar anisotropy is only one geodesic inside the correct matrix-valued shape space.

The strongest next object is consequently the intersection between a reflected-center scattering map and the Li–Liu Toda PE stress map, including all Hamilton and momentum equations. This is a materially better formulation than another finite spectral fit. It offers two outcomes of real value: a finite-amplitude matrix/twist mechanism that carries the center energy into an expanding end, or a rigorous incompatibility between the two stress maps. Even success would resolve only a negative four-dimensional module; peer work on the positive orbifold and collapse routes remains unfinished, and higher-dimensional quantifiers remain untouched.

## Deep-Reasoning

This step corrected three structural errors in the Step 76 scattering formulation and produced a genuinely stronger geometric bound. The most important correction distinguishes three geometric objects that had been conflated: the center metric q₀ at the reflection face S=0 (where R(q₀)=-6), the conformal infinity γ at the PE end r→∞ (where R_γ < -24 in the center-normalized gauge), and the transverse-traceless filling datum g₃ that carries all nonlocal information about the Einstein filling beyond the conformal class. Step 76 Section 9 incorrectly asked whether a Li-Liu boundary representative could have R = -6, conflating the center condition with a conformal infinity condition. The leading PE stress e^{2r}S° → Sch(γ)°♯ is determined by γ alone and does not distinguish fillings; the filling datum g₃ enters only at the next order through the renormalized stress e^{3r}[S° - Sch°♯ e^{-2r}] → -(3/2)γ⁻¹g₃.

The bound R_γ < -24 is the major quantitative improvement. The argument uses the standard ODE comparison: from H' = 3 - |S|² and |S|² ≥ H²/3 (Cauchy-Schwarz on a 3×3 positive semi-definite matrix), H ≤ 3 tanh(r) where 3 tanh is the solution of y' = 3 - y²/3 with y(0) = 0. Since e^{2r}·3(1-tanh r) → 6, the weighted deficit e^{2r}(3-H) → -R_γ/4 satisfies -R_γ/4 ≥ 6. Equality requires S = (H/3)I everywhere, giving the cosh-warped product g = dr² + cosh²(r)q₀ with Ric(q₀) = -2q₀. On T³ this forces constant sectional curvature -2/3, impossible by Preissmann. So R_γ < -24 strictly. Combined with the normal identity -R_γ/4 = 3 + ∫₀^∞ e^{2r}|S-I|²dr, the shear integral is at least 3.

The Fuchsian decomposition z(r) = e^{2r}(3-H) - 6e^{2r}/(e^{2r}+1) satisfies z' = ((u+w)/3 - 2)z + e^{2r}|P|² with z(0) = 0, so z ≥ 0 and -R_γ/4 = 6 + lim e^{2r}z(r). This cleanly separates the isotropic (Fuchsian cosh) contribution from the anisotropic stress P. The anisotropic contribution is strictly positive because the center theorem forces λ_min S'(0) ≤ -3 while tr S'(0) = 3.

The ASD obstruction was formalized: reflection across a totally geodesic T³ reverses orientation, forcing an ASD metric to have W = 0 near the hypersurface (by Einstein analyticity). This gives constant sec = -1, incompatible with a T³ level (Preissmann). So any reflected core must be non-ASD. The Li-Liu Type-I metrics are ASD and cannot serve as reflected-core fillings.

The TTCS verification confirmed all claims with three important caveats: (1) R_γ < -24 is for the center-normalized PE representative, not a conformal invariant; (2) the ASD obstruction needs explicit Einstein even-extension (which holds by the Cauchy data construction: q(0) = q₀, q'(0) = 0, and the equation's r→-r symmetry forces all odd jets to vanish); (3) e^{3r}S° diverges in general — only the renormalized expression with Sch subtracted is finite.

The verifier also corrected the near-center expansion: e^{2r}|S-I|² = 3 + (|S'|²-6)r² + O(r³), because the linear terms cancel (the -6r from |S-I|² is exactly compensated by the 6r from the e^{2r} = 1 + 2r + ... expansion times the constant 3). So the integral is 3ε + O(ε³), not 3ε - 3ε² as originally written.

The fundamental open question is now sharply stated: does there exist a non-ASD PE Einstein filling on (0,∞) × T³ whose backward evolution reaches S = 0? Anderson's Fredholm index 0 theory gives locally discrete fillings for fixed conformal class but no existence guarantee. The dimension count is balanced: center data and PE data each have two function degrees of freedom after gauge and constraints, so the problem is not obviously over-determined. The TTCS generator identified the defect route as potentially viable even if exact cores don't exist: weighted defect moments can remain O(1) as pointwise defect → 0 because the exponential weight e^{2r} amplifies small defects into finite renormalized stress. This means exact monotonicity or integral obstructions may not automatically yield approximate obstructions.

The positive branch has an important validation from A01: OSS/Tian confirm KE on Bl₅(P²) for the same-chirality desingularization, but the mixed-chirality #₃(S²×S²) is not Fano and the inter-node radial response at O(t³) is unresolved. A02's chiral ALE exclusion tightens the outermost model bound to |Γ| ≤ 4 on balanced rows.

The research state is: strong structural understanding of the negative graph-manifold route (R_γ < -24, ASD exclusion, three-object distinction, Fuchsian decomposition, dimensional balance) but the core existence question remains open. The non-ASD PE filling landscape on T³ is the key unexplored mathematical territory.

## Deep-Reasoning

The full Yau 26 statement remains unresolved: neither normalized sign branch has been settled in dimension four, no higher-dimensional reduction is valid, and no final Lean proof exists. This Step redirected the negative graph-manifold route from complete reflected PE fillings to the object actually needed by the construction: a finite vanishing-defect connector reaching the expanding-tail data of Step 73. The rotating-eigenframe Bianchi VII_0 family supplied a decisive inexpensive test. Although its torus slices are genuinely nonflat and its orbit axes rotate with z, its geometry still reduces to a one-dimensional anisotropy potential K=2k²a⁻²sinh²d. The reflected Hamilton identity forces K(0)=6+E_r−E_z−E_1−E_2, hence K(0)≥6−4δ when ||Ric+3g||op≤δ. The reduced equations u′+Hu=3−K−E_z, d″+Hd′=2K coth(d)−(E_1−E_2), and (log K)′=−2u+2 coth(d)d′ then form a protected region. For δ≤3/5, after choosing d(0)>0, every positive-radius point satisfies u=a′/a<0, d′>0, and K>K(0). The proof is independent of the sign of H because the damping terms vanish at the possible contact faces. Thus fixed helical rotation cannot convert the forced center contraction into expansion: ||S−I||op>1 and the slice Ricci norm remains greater than 6−4δ throughout any connected finite connector. This excludes a natural mechanism directly at the vanishing-defect level, rather than merely showing that an exact PE completion fails.

The obstruction also reveals what a successful connector must add. Rotation constrained to one fixed geodesic in the orbit-shape space retains positive feedback: contraction of a and growth of d both increase K. Escaping this feedback requires genuinely two-dimensional base transport, a full matrix-valued orbit map into SL(2,R)/SO(2) whose tension can turn in target space, nontrivial Hamilton–Codazzi transfer through off-diagonal shape components, or a parameter-dependent source whose pointwise norm vanishes while its weighted moment remains finite. These possibilities must be tested through the full Ricci system, not through prescribed intrinsic curvature or unconstrained shape evolution. A complete non-ASD PE metric remains a useful exact model but is not necessary for the graph construction. Likewise, an ordinary decaying Jacobi field on a Li–Liu cusp background normally preserves the cusp; opening that end would require a singularly translated transition that becomes order one in a receding region.

The Step also corrected the PE side calculation. Assuming a smooth global normal foliation from the reflected center to the PE end, Riccati comparison gives R_gamma(x)≤−24 for the center-normalized representative along each ray. Equality on one ray controls only that ray; Preissmann excludes equality everywhere, so strictness is established somewhere but not automatically at every boundary point. With u_H=3−H, w=3(1−tanh r), z=u_H−w, and Z=e^(2r)z, the consistent equation is Z′=((u_H+w)/3)Z+e^(2r)|P|² and −R_gamma/4=6+lim Z. These are necessary relations under the foliation assumption, not a general obstruction to finite forced connectors. On the positive side, standard #3(S²×S²) has b_+=3 and therefore cannot carry a positive Kähler–Einstein metric; the mixed-chirality desingularization requires a genuinely non-Kähler mechanism. The peer radial calculation remains mathematically useful, but only as a local test of that mechanism.

## Deep-Reasoning

This Step achieved a structural breakthrough in understanding the negative graph-manifold route for Yau Problem 26. The central mathematical discovery is that the orthogonally transitive T²-invariant Einstein system with Ric = −3g reduces to a **weighted harmonic map to H² = SL(2,ℝ)/SO(2)**, coupled to area and base conformal-factor equations. This reduction unifies all prior connector work—the Step 73 expanding tail, the Step 74/75 linearized mode analysis, the Step 76 center energy identities, and the Step 78 Bianchi VII₀ barrier—into a single coherent mathematical framework.

The structural equations are:
1. Area: Δ(eσ) = 6e^{2λ+σ} (Liouville-type, driven by Λ = −3)
2. Orbit: div(eσ M⁻¹dM) = 0 (weighted harmonic map to H²)
3. Conformal: Δλ = (|∇σ|² − e_{H²})/4
4. Constraints: one cross and one difference equation

The orbit equation in H² polar coordinates (d, ψ) yields:
- d-equation: div(eσ∇d) = eσ sinh(d)cosh(d)|∇ψ|² [positive source drives d outward]
- ψ-conservation: div(eσ sinh²(d)∇ψ) = 0 [angular momentum conservation]

All verified symbolically: det G = e^{2σ} (exact), tr(M⁻¹M_r) = 0 (traceless), tr((M⁻¹M_r)²) = 2·e_{H²,r} (energy identity), round cusp Ric_rr = −3/t² (exact), Step 73 tail equation v_rr+3v_r+e^{-2r}v_zz = 0 (recovered), Step 74 linearized mode ψ''+3ψ'−k²e^{-2r}ψ = 0 (recovered).

The mechanism analysis reveals WHY the VII₀ barrier holds and what escapes it. In VII₀, the orbit map is helicoidal: (d(r), kz) in H². The angular velocity ψ_z = k is frozen, making the d-equation source sinh(d)cosh(d)k² permanently positive and d monotonically increasing. In the general two-variable case, ψ(r,z) evolves via the conservation law and is NOT frozen. The angular gradient |∇ψ| can become small, removing the d-equation source. The growing weight eσ (driven by Λ = −3) enables this redistribution.

Critically, the TTCS verification exposed three important constraints beyond the structural escape:

(a) **Iwasawa sign correction**: The α-equation in Iwasawa coordinates has a NEGATIVE sign: div(eσ∇α) = −e^{σ−2α}|∇β|². This is consistent with the POSITIVE sign in polar coordinates because the Christoffel symbols differ. The diagonal case (β=0) is unaffected.

(b) **Convex distance maximum principle**: For EXACT Einstein metrics on a reflected cylinder with constant outer boundary, the orbit map must be constant. Proof: F(U) = ½d²_{H²}(U,P) satisfies Hess F ≥ g_{H²}, so div(ρ∇(F∘U)) ≥ ρ|dU|². Neumann center + Dirichlet exit = 0 forces U ≡ P. This is a genuine obstruction to exact connectors.

(c) **Matrix Noether flow**: The full sl(2,ℝ)-valued conservation Q(r) = ∫ ρ M⁻¹M_r dz ≡ 0 is stronger than the scalar angular flux.

The maximum principle means the connector MUST be approximate (||E|| → 0, not E = 0). For approximate connectors, the forced orbit equation is div(ρ M⁻¹dM) = −2e^{2λ}ρ E°_orbit. Even as ||E||_∞ → 0, the weighted forcing e^{2λ}ρ||E|| ∼ e^{4r}δ can remain O(1) on long expanding connectors, potentially overcoming the maximum principle.

A zero-mode estimate gives the needed connector length: for a diagonal transition with d(r) = d₀(1−χ(r/R)), the orbit defect is O(d₀/R). Setting δ = d₀/R gives R = d₀/δ. For graph lattice parameter N with d₀ = 2 log N, the connector length R ∼ (2 log N)/δ grows logarithmically in N and inversely in δ.

The decisive open question is now precisely stated: can a sequence of approximate long connectors with ||E||_op → 0 transfer the center's O(1) orbit energy to the Step 73 tail interface while satisfying all constraints (Hamilton, momentum, base)? The answer determines the negative branch of Yau 26 for extended graph four-manifolds.

For the positive branch: A01's Green-response computation for the mixed-chirality desingularization and the corrected automorphism removal are the active analytical tools. The #₃(S²×S²) case cannot be positive Kähler–Einstein (b₊ = 3), so any result requires a non-Kähler mechanism.

## Deep-Reasoning

The full Yau 26 problem remains unresolved: neither normalized sign has been settled in dimension four, there is no valid all-dimensional reduction, and no complete Lean formalization exists. This Step applied computational pressure to the negative graph-manifold route at its actual missing interface rather than repeating the solved expanding tail. The Step 79 cusp-based budget was corrected in three consequential ways. A zero-mode transition on a fixed cusp does not begin at a reflected scalar-minus-six center; in physical radius the invariant orbit-source measure is ρ dvol(γ_B), equal to e^{3r}drdz on the round cusp rather than e^{4r}drdz; and common N^{-2} scaling of both orbit directions changes σ by a constant while leaving the normalized orbit map U unchanged, so it does not generate a transport distance 2 log N.

The invariant base equation was verified symbolically against the direct four-dimensional Ricci tensor:

This Step achieved three rigorously verified structural results and two TTCS-corrected theoretical insights for the reflected Einstein evolution from T²-invariant centers on T³.

The first discovery is the exact S'(0) eigenvalue formula: Spec = {-3, 3±√(3(k²+12))}. The z-eigenvalue -3 is universal for ALL constant-area R=-6 centers, regardless of loop shape. The orbit split L = √(3(k²+12)) = 6 coth(d*) grows with k: higher winding numbers produce faster orbit contraction (-3.93 for k=2 up to -12.10 for k=8). This formula was derived by TTCS using n·n' = J, (cosh d n' - sinh d J)² = I, and the traceless property A² = (|A|²/2)I = 3I. The matching with numerics to 4 digits confirms both the analytical derivation and the parametrization convention.

The second result is the corrected angular-slip analysis. The energy trace cancellation |U_z|² = 12 + ε²[q²sin²-(2k²+12)cos²] + O(ε³) is exact, with coefficient 20 for k=2, q=1. But the TTCS correction is essential: the angular slip does NOT preserve the full orbit Ricci to O(ε). The traceless part of Q' = M⁻¹M_zz changes at O(ε), meaning S'(0) orbit eigenvalues shift at O(ε) even while the z-eigenvalue shifts only at O(ε²). The B₀ condition cancels only the scalar-energy first variation, not the full tensor.

The third result is the volume-weighted universal contraction: ⟨u'(0)⟩_ρ = -3 for ANY area profile (constant or not). The proof uses ⟨ḣ⟩_ρ = -⟨h²⟩_ρ from integration by parts with ρ̇ = hρ. This is stronger than the non-weighted -3+⟨h²⟩ result (which applies to arclength, not geometric volume). The coupling constraint e = 12-4ḣ-3h² ≥ 0 limits area variation.

The fourth result is the rigorous VII₀ collapse: K≥6 → H≤√3 → -u grows like √3(1-e^{-√3r}) → K grows past 10 → H' ≤ -1-H² → finite-time blowup. This applies to all winding numbers (numerically: r_c = 0.24-0.36 for k=2,...,8).

The critical fifth finding is the TTCS-identified scope limitation: the VII₀ collapse uses K as a single scalar with monotone feedback, but the full z-dependent OT system has div(ρ M⁻¹∇M) = 0 with flux redistribution between r and z directions, subject to the Noether constraint ∫ρ M⁻¹M_r dz = 0. This breaks the scalar monotone mechanism. The collapse is NOT proven for the general z-dependent case.

The decisive open question is now precisely stated: does the full coupled (γ_B, σ, M) system admit a weighted monotone functional that inherits the VII₀ positive feedback? The natural candidates are: (a) the convex distance integral F = ∫ρ d²_{H²}(U,P) dz (whose evolution involves Hess(d²) ≥ g_{H²} but also base-metric and area response terms), (b) the total orbit energy ∫ρ e_{H²} dz, and (c) the matrix Noether current. Testing these against the coupled equations is the highest-value next computation.

For the positive branch: A02's three-leg audit correctly identifies that λ=0 (generic SO(4)) and λ<0 remain open legs. A01's corrected Green-mode calculation found a live chirality channel but not the full coefficient. A02's near-pinched A1 construction gives ||Ric-σg|| ≤ C/|log a| but is only a positive-input construction.

The overall problem structure: the negative branch needs either a monotone quantity closing the OT class, or a z-dependent connector construction. The positive branch needs the complete Green transfer or an alternative obstruction mechanism. Neither branch is closed.

## Deep-Reasoning

The negative graph-manifold route is now organized around a specific physical reversal variable rather than a generic monotone functional. For Gaussian OT slices, K = ⟨|U_s|² − h²⟩ satisfies ⟨R(q_r)⟩ = −K/2 and x′ = 3 − K/2 − ⟨E_zz⟩ − x(x+y), where x = I/V is mean horizontal expansion. A reflected scalar-minus-six center has K(0)=12 and x′(0)=−3, while any first return x=0 with x′≥0 and ||E||op≤δ requires K≤6+2δ. Thus a connector must lower this intrinsic spatial orbit-energy excess by about six units. Independent tensor calculation further gives K′(0)=0 and K″(0)=72+2⟨|τ|²⟩+(3/8)Var(k)≥72, so every exact reflected OT germ first moves in the wrong direction. A successful connector, if it exists, must undergo an intermediate-radius nonlinear turnover rather than being produced by favorable center jets.

The exact production identity is K′=−2⟨τ,b⟩+2⟨vc⟩+Cov(v−u,k)−2xK. Before a first return, x<0, so −2xK is positive and resists the required energy drop. Codazzi gives D_s v=h(u−v/2)−(1/2)⟨U_s,b⟩−E_rs, identifying radial orbit transport, area variation, and covariance as the remaining possible mechanisms. An explicit orbit-defect term must not be added while τ is retained; it appears once, with the corresponding sign, only after τ is eliminated using the orbit equation.

The integrated balances alone cannot prohibit reversal. Algebraically favorable slices exist, and a flat homogeneous exact Einstein germ with u=0 and orbit rate p=√3 has u′=3, showing that local Einstein geometry permits horizontal reversal away from reflection. The unresolved mathematics is therefore reachability from the prescribed reflected center while K first rises, later falls below roughly six, and all Einstein components remain small without curvature concentration. This sharply distinguishes the general OT problem from the VII₀ collapse mechanism.

The full Yau 26 problem remains open. Even a negative graph connector would still require global attachment and would not settle the positive normalized branch or higher-dimensional quantifiers. A01 also withdrew its proposed positive-side Green-response positivity after identifying a negative TT mode and singular self-pairings; only a flat principal odd identity and a matched regularized relative-response problem remain there. No complete proof, disproof, or Lean formalization has been obtained.

## Deep-Reasoning

This step achieved a precise determination of what the K-production framework can and cannot establish, through rigorous TTCS verification that corrected several sign-analysis errors and an independent generator search for monotone functionals.

The corrected sign structure: after eliminating τ via the orbit equation and expanding vc via Codazzi, the production Φ decomposes into six groups. Only ONE is proven non-negative: the IBP orbit-velocity term ∫m[f'+2(x+y)f]dr = m(R)f(R) + ∫2ymf dr ≥ 0, using y ≥ 0 (itself proven from the y' equation for δ < 3). The remaining five groups — Cov(H,|b|²), ⟨h²(v-2u)⟩, tension ⟨h⟨A,b⟩⟩, Cov(v-u,k), and forcing — are all indefinite. My initial classification had incorrectly placed Cov(H,|b|²) and the circle-geometry term in the positive group; the TTCS verifier caught both errors by noting that only average (not pointwise) sign control is available.

The corrected budget: ∫mΦ dr ≤ m(R)(6+2δ) - 12 ≤ -6+2δ. The claimed -18 required an unproven P_orb ≥ 12. The center jet coefficient [⟨|τ|²⟩ + 3Var(k)/16] can vanish for certain centers, so no universal early-production lower bound exists.

The TTCS generator conducted a systematic search through orbit energy, squared distance, Noether current, finite-moment combinations, and Bochner/Bakry-Émery routes. None yields a monotone quantity excluding the K-drop. The orbit energy evolution contains sign-indefinite stress-velocity exchange. The squared-distance functional gives flux monotonicity Ψ' ≥ 0 (recovering Step 79's constant-exit obstruction) but NOT slice-distance monotonicity. The Noether constraint Q ≡ 0 is finite-dimensional only. The finite-moment system (K,x,y,⟨|b|²⟩,⟨h²⟩) does not close because local correlations and stress terms introduce irreducible new quantities.

The Bakry-Émery analysis revealed a structural limitation: on the round cusp with σ = 2r, the exact Einstein identity gives Ric^σ_B = diag(-1, -1+2tanh r) in orthonormal frame. The radial eigenvalue is universally -1. Orbit stress improves only the tangential direction. Therefore Bochner-type arguments can at most give exponential growth bounds (from Ric^σ ≥ -1), not sign-definite Lyapunov control.

A02's message #599 provides the deepest structural reduction so far: Yau-26 false in dimension n (≥3) requires a no-Einstein manifold in that dimension. This uses Lohkamp (every closed manifold carries Ric < 0) plus rescaling into [c,0] for any c < 0. For n ≥ 5, no certified no-Einstein manifold exists, so refutation is currently impossible. This makes all negative-branch work necessarily 4-dimensional.

The combined picture: the graph-manifold connector problem is at a genuine mathematical fork. The K-production identity, VII₀ collapse, constant-exit obstruction, and universal initial worsening all constrain the solution but do not close it. No monotone functional, Lyapunov argument, or Bochner estimate excludes the K-drop. The escape mechanisms (phase flip, area gradient growth, weight redistribution, covariance engineering, Noether-compatible oscillation) are precisely identified but their sufficiency is unknown.

For the positive branch, A01's K-symmetry theorem reduces the mixed-chirality problem to a finite smooth off-diagonal odd-odd Green kernel whose sign is undetermined.

The research stands at a decision point: continue refinement of the OT connector analysis (which has reached a genuine impasse at the analytic level), attempt a full numerical resolution of the Koiso germ evolution, or reconsider the approach entirely in light of A02's reduction.

## Deep-Reasoning

Step 83’s route assessment required a substantive reversal. For the weighted orbit equation with L=Δ+⟨∇σ,∇·⟩=ρ⁻¹div(ρ∇·), the relevant drift curvature in the harmonic-map Bochner formula is Ric_B−Hess σ, not Ric_B+Hess σ. Substitution of the exact base equation gives Ric_B−Hess σ=−3γ_B+(1/2)dσ⊗dσ+(1/2)U*h_H²+E_B. Thus the same orbit stress that drives the coupled Einstein response contributes positively inside the Bochner curvature term; Step 83’s negative-eigenvalue argument did not test this structure.

Writing A=U*h_H² for the Gram tensor of dU, the base-stress contribution is (1/2)tr(A²). Since the target H² has curvature −1, its Bochner contribution is 2det A=(tr A)²−tr(A²). Their sum is Q(A)=(tr A)²−(1/2)tr(A²). If the nonnegative eigenvalues of A are λ₁,λ₂, then Q=(λ₁²+λ₂²)/2+2λ₁λ₂ and therefore (1/2)|dU|⁴≤Q≤(3/4)|dU|⁴. This is a real coercive quartic term, not merely a favorable sign in one base direction. The remaining linear background contribution −3|dU|² permits a threshold phenomenon rather than immediate positivity, while the dσ term is also nonnegative. For an approximate connector, the derivative of the weighted tension should be retained until integration by parts: ∫η²ρ⟨dU,Dτ_σ⟩ becomes −∫η²ρ|τ_σ|² plus cutoff or boundary pairings. This avoids differentiating the Ricci defect and creates another favorable term. Whether these terms control the negative K-production correlations or instead force concentration and boundary flux is now a precise open question.

The correct exact benchmark is γ_B=dr²+e^{2r}dz², σ=2r. It has Ric_B−Hess σ=diag(−1,−3) in an orthonormal frame, exactly matching −3γ_B+(1/2)dσ². Step 83 instead used dr²+cosh²(r)dz² with the same σ; its base defect is diag(0,2−2tanh r), so it is not an exact Einstein benchmark. A second correction removes the proposed nonconstant closed geodesic in H². Every smooth nonconstant closed center loop has nonzero tension. Convexity may yield a quantitative tension floor once the actual circle length, speed, area profile, and admissible self-intersections are fixed, but this has not yet been established and would not by itself provide a uniform radial persistence scale.

A late peer message opened a complementary negative-branch route. The retrieved Besson–Courtois–Gallot rigidity source states that if a closed manifold Y maps to a hyperbolic N with degree d and Ric_Y≥−3g in dimension four, then Vol(Y)≥|d|Vol(N); its Corollary 1.7 gives a strict fixed-target volume separation for N#N. Sambusetti’s result excludes every Einstein metric on N#N. Combining the degree-two BCG bound with Chern–Gauss–Bonnet gives a particularly sharp scale for near-negative pinching. If χ=χ(N), V_N=4π²χ/3, M=N#N, and ||Ric_g+3g||op≤δ, rescaling by a=1+δ/3 yields Vol(g)≥2V_N/a². Meanwhile χ(M)=2χ−2 and Chern–Gauss–Bonnet gives Vol(g)≤8π²(2χ−2)/(6−4δ−(4/3)δ²). Compatibility therefore requires χ(8δ+2δ²)≥6+4δ+(2/3)δ². In particular δ is at least asymptotically 3/(4χ). This calculation still needs an independent normalization check, but it explains the peer’s O(1/χ) target. It does not construct the required sequence: a disproof of the negative branch would need hyperbolic connected-sum metrics attaining defect O(1/χ) along covers with χ→∞.

The quantifier-level picture was also corrected. A no-Einstein manifold is necessary for a counterexample in a fixed dimension, but this is not an equivalence. Lohkamp plus scaling shows that such a manifold defeats intervals of the form [c,0]; it does not by itself defeat arbitrary narrow negative or positive intervals. A two-sign counterexample in dimension four would already disprove the universal statement, whereas higher-dimensional examples are not additionally required. Higher-dimensional no-Einstein manifolds remain a legitimate research question: Case’s 2022 six-dimensional paper explicitly says no higher-dimensional unrestricted obstruction was then known and that its proposed diffeomorphism invariant is not known to be finite on any example. This supports a historical frontier statement, not a theorem that such manifolds do not exist. Likewise, A01’s symmetry result remains a local desingularization/kernel result until a separate implication to same-manifold Einstein nonexistence is proved.

The full Yau 26 problem remains unresolved. The strongest new opportunity is a two-level negative investigation: use the corrected drift-stress Bochner identity to understand connector transport locally, while using the BCG–Chern–Gauss–Bonnet calculation to identify the globally necessary O(1/χ) scale on N#N. These mechanisms may meet in a controlled hyperbolic-to-hyperbolic neck construction, but neither existence nor impossibility has yet been established.

## Deep-Reasoning

This step achieved a qualitative breakthrough in the OT connector problem by correcting the weighted Bochner convention that Step 83 had wrong. The drift Laplacian L = Δ + ⟨∇σ,∇·⟩ has curvature Ric_B − Hess σ (not +Hess σ). Substituting the Einstein base equation gives Ric_B − Hess σ = −3γ + ½dσ² + ½U*h + E_B, where the orbit-stress ½U*h_{H²} and the dσ term are both nonneg. The H² target curvature (K = −1) contributes +2det(A). Combined: ½Le = |DdU|² + ½|dU(∇σ)|² + Q(A) − 3e + E_B·A, where Q = ½tr(A²) + 2det(A) ≥ ½e² by the algebraic identity Q − ½e² = det(A) = λ₁λ₂ ≥ 0. Dropping nonneg terms: ½Le ≥ ½e(e−6).

The maximum principle on a reflected compact connector gives sup e ≤ max{6, sup_{exit} e}. TTCS independently verified all claims and corrected the center identity: the tangential orbit-area log-derivative h = (log ρ)_s is not the radial mean curvature H = u+v; while H(0) = 0 by reflection, h(0,z) need not vanish. The correct identity is ⟨e(0,·)⟩_μ = K(0) + ⟨h²⟩ = 12 + ⟨h²⟩ ≥ 12, which strengthens rather than weakens the contradiction. If exit e < 12, then sup e < 12, but ⟨e(0,·)⟩ ≥ 12 > sup e — impossible since a positive-measure average cannot exceed the supremum.

This eliminates the exact reflected OT Einstein connector. Every exact connector requires exit orbit energy density sup_{exit} e ≥ 12, incompatible with the Step 73 expanding tail (e → 0). The result strictly generalizes Step 79's constant-exit obstruction and explains why all K-production searches and numerical experiments found only apparent obstructions: the exact problem has no solution.

For the forced case, the tension identity ⟨dU, Dτ_σ⟩ = div_σ(V) − |τ_σ|² was verified. This converts the forced Bochner to ½Le = |DdU|² + div_σ(V) − |F|² + Q − 3e + nonneg + E_B·A. The div_σ(V) term is the precise obstacle: it involves DF (derivatives of forcing), preventing a direct pointwise maximum principle. The integrated form removes the divergence via ∫η²ρ div_σ(V) = −2∫ηρ V(∇η), converting the DF-dependent term into controllable V-coefficient cross terms.

A02's warped waist barrier (#614) establishes δ ≥ 3/2 for all warped-product turnarounds with nonneg fiber curvature, independently verified by A01 (#617). This and the Bochner comparison are complementary: Bochner covers the full non-warped OT class but only in the exact case; the warped waist covers warped products with any defect level. Combined, only non-warped forced connectors remain as a possible construction.

The decisive next question is whether the integrated Bochner + De Giorgi–Moser iteration gives a universal bound sup e ≤ 6 + C'δ with C' independent of the connector length R. The standard theory handles the div_σ(V) term as a divergence-form perturbation with L²-controlled coefficient, and the Sobolev constant on the 2D weighted base with Ric_σ ≥ −3 is universal. If this closes, then 12 − 8δ ≤ 6 + C'δ forces δ ≥ 6/(8+C') > 0, giving a universal graph-route defect threshold. For N#N, the BCG deficit is additive (no uniform δ₀), so that route is not blocked by this alone and remains open with non-warped S³ necks.

## Deep-Reasoning

Step 86 changed the forced OT problem from a presumed routine Moser iteration into a precise coupled localization problem. The Step 85 exact comparison remains valid: an exact reflected free-T² OT Einstein connector with a low-energy exit is impossible. For an approximate connector, however, the traceless orbit equation gives the invariant relation τ_σ(U)↔−2Ê₀ and |τ_σ(U)|≤2δ when ‖Ric+3g‖op≤δ; the large factor in conformal coordinates is only the weighted-coordinate density. The correct local geometry is finite-dimensional: Ric_f^4=Ric_B−Hess σ−(1/2)dσ⊗dσ=−3γ_B+(1/2)U*h+E_B≥−(3+δ)γ_B. It supports normalized effective-four-dimensional local estimates, but not an unnormalized Sobolev constant independent of weighted volume.

The decisive correction is in the superlevel weak equation. Testing with η²u, u=(e−k)+, produces both −∫η²⟨V,∇u⟩ and −2∫ηu⟨V,∇η⟩. The first term was absent from the prior handoff. With |F|≤f₀, ‖E_B‖op≤b₀ and Ψ(e)=e(e−6)/2−b₀e−f₀², Kato gives the nonsingular gradient coefficient a_k=(3e−k)/(4e)∈[1/2,3/4). The natural positive root is k*=3+b₀+√((3+b₀)²+2f₀²), and at u=e−k* the reaction is exactly Su²+u³/2. For b₀=δ and f₀=2δ, k*=6+2δ+(4/3)δ²+O(δ³). Low exit energy therefore gives global Dirichlet, L², and L³ control of the excess proportional to the weighted measure of its own support. This is real coercivity, but normalized local Moser estimates still require localization of that excess; they do not automatically yield the near-sharp ceiling 6+O(δ). A C⁰-small tension can have a large derivative in a layer of thickness comparable to δe^(−3/2), and scalar weak models realize the same divergence-forcing escape without satisfying the full OT system.

The most important new structure combines orbit energy with orbit-area growth. The trace equation is Lσ=6−T, T=tr_orb E. For W=e+c|∇σ|² and J=V−cT∇σ, the independently verified inequality is ½LW≥div_σJ+W²/[2(1+c)]−(3+δ)W−D_c(δ)+P, where D_c=12cδ+4(c+1)δ² and P is an explicit nonnegative sum containing |DdU|², c|Hess σ|², det A, orbit stress, and c(e−|∇σ|²)²/[2(1+c)]. Moreover P≥|∇W|²/(4W), while the exact vertical eigenvalue relation sharpens the flux bound to |J|≤2δ max{1,√c}√W. At c=1/2 the zero-defect reaction level is 9, below the reflected-center average at least 12; its perturbed root is 9+5δ+(8/9)δ²+O(δ³). Thus incorporating the area equation creates a larger order-one separation than the orbit energy alone.

Area expansion also links this combined energy to global propagation. If W≤B on a free-OT domain, then Lσ≥6−2δ and |∇σ|≤√(B/c) imply a Dirichlet weighted Cheeger lower bound h_μ≥(6−2δ)√(c/B), hence λ₁^Dir(−L)≥c(6−2δ)²/(4B). Without a global bound, each regular relatively compact superlevel component Ω_t still satisfies P_μ(Ω_t)≥(6−2δ)√(c/t)μ(Ω_t). This matches the exact round-cusp benchmark, where the radial Dirichlet spectrum tends to 9/4 rather than zero as collar length grows. The resulting bootstrap is not yet closed: its global spectral estimate depends on B, and a coarse scalar layer can balance an O(W²) reaction by an O(δ√W) flux over thickness O(δW^(−3/2)). What may exclude that layer is precisely what the scalar model omits: the gradient coercivity, the target-map Maurer–Cartan integrability, the sharp trace/traceless defect relation, and the horizontal Einstein constraints. Establishing their combined effect, or constructing them compatibly, is now the difficult center of this restricted negative-branch route.

These results concern reflected, free-T², orthogonally transitive connectors only. Approximate twist, singular orbits, general graph metrics, and the S³ necks of N#N remain outside this reduction. The positive normalized branch and the full dimension-dependent Yau-26 statement remain unresolved, and no Lean formalization has begun.

## Deep-Reasoning

This step achieved the primary quantitative obstruction that the forced Bochner program has been building toward since Step 84. The key mathematical advance is replacing the local superlevel/Moser program (Step 86) with a global massive-resolvent comparison on a complete extension. The argument chain: (1) the forced Bochner inequality from Steps 85-86 gives (-L+κ)e ≤ κ²+8δ²-2div_σ V; (2) the CD(-(3+δ),4) curvature-dimension condition from the Einstein base equation; (3) the Riccati Fisher information bound I(t) ≤ NK/(1-e^{-2Kt}) under CD(-K,N), which the TTCS correctly identified as replacing the naive N/(2t)+NK/2 that fails for large t on the round cusp; (4) the resolvent gradient estimate C_κ = 2/√(3+δ) via the Beta function B(1,1/2)=2; (5) the Duhamel semigroup comparison principle; and (6) the self-consistent quadratic closure B ≤ α+β√B contradicting the center floor 12-8δ for δ < δ* ≈ 0.246.

The Fisher correction was essential: the naive bound gives I(t)→6 as t→∞ on the round cusp, but the actual radial Fisher information is 9+1/(2t)→9. ## Deep-Reasoning

Step 88 identified reflection as inessential to the strongest current free-T² orthogonally transitive obstruction. For a quotient cylinder B with orbit area ρ=e^σ, the volume of an invariant hypersurface over a closed base curve C is the length of C in the auxiliary metric ρ²γ_B. If both ends are exact outward-expanding cusp ends, this auxiliary metric is complete and proper, while lengths in the primitive essential loop class diverge at either end. A shortest primitive representative is therefore a smooth embedded geodesic, and its lift Σ is an invariant minimal T³. The outward orientation on both ends is indispensable: a contracting end makes primitive loop lengths tend to zero and allows the infimum to escape.

The separator geometry was derived with fixed normal and measure conventions. For E=Ric+3g, D=tr E−2E(ν,ν), h=σ_s, e_s=|U_s|², and averages with weight ρ ds, minimality and contracted Gauss give R_Σ=−6+D−|II|². The intrinsic scalar formula for ds²+G(s) is R_Σ=−2h_s−3h²/2−e_s/2. Periodic weighted integration yields the exact identity ⟨e_s⟩=12−2⟨D⟩+2⟨|II|²⟩+⟨h²⟩. Since |D|≤4δ and the full base energy e dominates e_s, every such separator forces sup e≥12−8δ. The additional second-fundamental-form term strengthens rather than weakens the former reflected-center floor.

The massive-resolvent ceiling from Step 87 contains no reflection input. Under the complete free-OT equations and CD(−(3+δ),4), it remains sup e≤B(δ), where B(δ)=[4δ/√(3+δ)+√(2(3+δ)+20δ²/(3+δ))]². The heat-kernel calculation was corrected in the durable files to state C_κ≤2/√(3+δ), not equality; the subsequent ceiling uses only this upper estimate. Combining floor and ceiling excludes the complete two-ended free-OT geometry for δ<0.246249763690668…. Thus nonreflection alone is no longer a viable escape within this class.

A further structural observation is that the minimal-separator floor itself survives connection twist. Restricting a free invariant connection to a one-dimensional base curve makes it locally gauge-trivial; translation holonomy does not alter the intrinsic scalar formula or reduced measure. Twist can evade the present theorem only by changing the upper Bochner/resolvent comparison. A newly retrieved primary source, Liu’s toric Einstein analysis, gives the mixed Ricci formula and constant exact twist scalars: α_a=ρ⟨[X,Y/μ],V_a⟩ is constant for an exact Einstein metric. An exact OT open end therefore forces exact twist to vanish throughout the connected free region. Merely asymptotic OT ends can still carry nonzero conserved twist while physical connection curvature decays, and approximate Einstein metrics control dα_a with growing weights rather than α_a pointwise. This makes the variable-fibre Abelian reduction the precise next object.

The clean-context twist formulas suggest favorable connection-curvature contributions to base drift curvature and separator |II|², but adverse traceless vertical forcing and tension-square terms in the orbit-map Bochner equation. Their coefficients were not adopted because the available fixed-fibre bundle formula does not establish the full variable-G system. The next advance requires a direct tensor derivation. The diffuse non-OT, non-warped S³-neck mechanism on N#N remains untouched; local torus and waist results cannot exclude volume-scale spreading. Peer corrections were incorporated on the positive side as well: the product curvature target is rank one, odd gauge invariance is useful, but the proposed order-t³ mixed-chirality obstruction still requires the physical singular-field response, all interacting terms, frame motion, and a remainder smaller than order t³. None of these restricted results resolves both normalized signs, arbitrary metrics, or the all-dimensional Yau 26 statement.

## Deep-Reasoning

Step 89 achieved the complete variable-fibre T² reduction with twist and resolved a critical sign propagation issue that initially threatened to reverse the twist's effect on the Bochner obstruction.

The central mathematical advance: for a free T²-invariant metric g = \gamma_B + G_{ab}(d\xi^a+A^a)(d\xi^b+A^b) with G=e^\sigma M, the twist F^a = dA^a modifies the Ricci tensor in three blocks. A full symbolic SymPy computation of the 4D Ricci tensor for g = e^{2\lambda}(dr^2+dz^2) + e^{\sigma+\alpha}(d\xi_1+Pdz)^2 + e^{\sigma-\alpha}d\xi_2^2 established: (1) orbit twist Ricci = (1/2)G_{ac}G_{bd}f^cf^d (factor 1/2, verified ratio = 1/2 exactly); (2) direct base twist Ricci = -Q\gamma_B (negative sign, verified ratio = -1 exactly); (3) orbit trace gives area equation L\sigma = 6+Q; (4) orbit traceless gives |S_F|^2 = Q^2 for diagonal one-charge case.

The critical sign issue: I initially concluded that since the direct base Ricci is -Q\gamma, the drift curvature must be -(3+Q)\gamma + ..., making the Bochner reaction weaker (e-6-2Q). This was WRONG. The full horizontal Einstein equation is Ric_B - Hess\sigma - (1/2)d\sigma^2 - (1/2)A - Q\gamma = -3\gamma, so solving gives Ric_B - Hess\sigma = (-3+Q)\gamma + (1/2)d\sigma^2 + (1/2)A. The -Q on the left becomes +Q on the right. The drift curvature is therefore Ric^\sigma = (-3+Q)\gamma + (1/2)A, and the Bochner reaction is e - 6 + 2Q, which is FAVORABLE.

The TTCS verifier caught this sign propagation error with a clean derivation, correctly identifying that the reaction contains +2Q not -2Q, and that the effective curvature parameter is K = 3-Q (improved, not worsened). The TTCS also confirmed that the Step 88 generator's final formulas were correct despite its own sloppy intermediate reasoning.

## Deep-Reasoning

Step 90 revised the free-T² direction at its decisive unresolved point. Exact Maxwell conservation removes twist from an exact orthogonally transitive open end only when the metric is Einstein throughout the connected region. For an approximately Einstein connector, mixed Ricci defect sources the charge, so Step 89's constant-Q resolvent curve cannot close the forced problem. The three quantities Q_-=inf Q, Q_+=sup Q, and the separator average Q_C govern different parts of the geometry and cannot be merged: Q_- enters the curvature-dimension estimate, Q_+ enters tension and flux size, and Q_C raises the minimal-separator energy floor. Exact OT ends imply Q_-=0, leaving the uniform curvature parameter at 3+δ rather than improving it.

The twist energy has a stronger internal structure than an arbitrary source. For Q=(1/2)e^{-3σ}q^T M^{-1}q on H², symbolic calculation established Hess_H Q=Qh and |grad_H Q|²=Q², while the vertical traceless equation gives S_F=-grad_H Q. Consequently <dU,D S_F>=-Qe+3X+R_q, with |X|≤|grad σ|Q√e and |R_q|≤√(2Qe)|b|. The -Qe term cancels pointwise with the +Qe supplied by the Einstein-solved horizontal drift curvature. Thus twist is not simply favorable: after expansion, its leading linear reaction disappears and the remaining area-charge exchange and charge derivative carry the difficulty. The mixed equation has the exact normalization dq=±2ρ*E_mix and |b|²=4|E_mix|²_HS, so ||E||op≤δ gives |b|≤2√2δ. On a round expanding cusp the physical amplitude w=e^{-(3σ+α)/2}q obeys w'+3w=b; sustained small forcing permits w=O(δ), while coordinate charge may change at order δe^{3r}.

Combining the orbit, charge, and area equations without differentiating E singles out W=e+2Q+3|grad σ|². Its first-order exchanges cancel and its flux is O(δ√W), but its zero-order part is not coercive for large Q: at a common critical point compatible with exact second jets, the nonflux contribution is 54-2Q². This explains structurally why neither the constant-mass resolvent nor a local maximum argument controls a concentrated charged core. A TTCS suggestion that an average Q=O(δ²) could close the argument was not adopted because it first assumes the unavailable e ceiling and does not convert global average control into the kernel-weighted control required by the resolvent.

The execution then exposed a concrete alternative mechanism. In the radial reduction γ=dr²+ψ²dθ², M=diag(e^α,e^{-α}), q=(q0,0), the exact constant-charge equations are u'=6+Q-u²-Hu, v'=Q-Hv-uv, K=-3+Q+Hu, and H'=-K-H². Smooth-center data have u=((6+Q0)/2)r+O(r³), v=(Q0/2)r+O(r³), H=r^{-1}-(Q0/2)r+O(r³), and K(0)=3Q0/2. The unused horizontal equation C=E_rr propagates exactly by C'=-2(u+H)C, so a regular center with C=0 solves the full reduced Einstein system. Numerical continuations for Q0=0.1,1,3,10,30,100 all reached r=4 and approached u=2, v=0, H=1, K=-1, Q=0; for Q0=100, Q fell below 10^{-2} by r≈0.982 and below 10^{-4} by r≈1.720. These runs establish the mechanism over the sampled range, while the local regular family permits every finite Q0.

After switching when w=δ, a forced collar with b=-A sin²(πs/L) was shot to w(L)=0. Across Q0=1,10,100, δ=0.1,0.03,0.01, and L=0.5,1,2, all 27 runs succeeded. The required amplitude was max|b|=C(L)δ, with C≈1.75–1.85, 0.365–0.395, and 0.0266–0.0293 respectively. The remaining horizontal constraint satisfies C'=-2(u+H)C-wb and was O(δ²). In this rank-one model the only defect blocks are C and the mixed component |b|/2, hence every sampled collar had ||Ric+3g||op<0.925δ. This rules out a local principle asserting that one exact OT end and small mixed Ricci defect force small interior Q.

The same constraint law isolates the next obstruction. A monotone discharge with w≥0 and b≤0 necessarily leaves C(L)>0 because C(L)=-e^{-2I(L)}∫e^{2I}wb. Endpoint smoothing alone cannot produce an exact Einstein attachment. A sign-changing two-mode pilot imposed w(L)=C(L)=0 algebraically, but required max|b|≈26δ for Q0=10, δ=0.03, L=1; this demonstrates controllability in one inefficient basis, not small-defect feasibility or a lower bound. The radial quotient is a disk rather than the two-ended cylinder required by the minimal-separator theorem, although the fibre T² action remains free. Generalized Einstein Dehn filling supplies a closely related exact benchmark: the toral black-hole metric on D²×T² is Einstein and asymptotic to a hyperbolic cusp. It confirms the charged-cap geometry but caps one cusp and produces an Einstein-bearing topology, so it does not supply the desired no-Einstein graph connector.

The negative free-T² frontier has therefore moved from an incorrectly presumed resolvent closure to a global two-end matching problem. The strongest next object is a cylindrical charged throat joining asymptotics (u,H,v,w)=(-2,-1,0,0) and (2,1,0,0), with flat endpoint jets and full operator Ricci defect tending to zero. Either such a throat can exploit charge redshift while satisfying both Maxwell and horizontal moment equations, or the two-end topology and minimal separator enforce a new global identity. This remains only a symmetry-class problem; diffuse non-OT S³ necks remain untouched. The positive branch is independently at the corrected tensor-sector determinantal response problem communicated by A02: the missing quantities are the Q-channel responses q_diag and q_adj, not the superseded scalar mixed-chirality interpretation. No result in this Step proves or disproves the full sign-unrestricted, all-dimensional Yau 26 statement, and no final Lean formalization is warranted.

## Deep-Reasoning

Step 91 established three verified geometric results for the free-T² connector problem and identified a structural curvature-energy tradeoff that constrains the z-dependent frontier.

The flat-slice barrier is the cleanest result: any cohomogeneity-one (radial) charged metric on a cylindrical base has constant-coefficient T³ r-level sets, hence R(q_r)=0. The contracted Gauss then gives H²≥9−6δ, preventing H from crossing zero for δ<3/2. This kills the entire Step 90 radial cylindrical control program — the disk cap avoids it because ψ(0)=0 collapses the angular circle, but the cylindrical topology cannot.

The separator stability with twist is the central new identity. Using the O'Neill/Koszul formula for the horizontal-vertical connection, the twist energy Q contributes exactly Q to |II|² through the off-diagonal terms II(e_T,e_α)=(ε/2)√G_{αα}f^α. TTCS verified this with both branches, including the sign convention (ε=±1 from orientation, but |II|²_twist = Q regardless). Combined with the second variation φ=1 on the stable minimal separator, this gives ⟨|II|²⟩≤3+δ and hence Q_C≤3+δ. The separator floor becomes ⟨e_s⟩≥12−8δ+2Q_C, with the coefficient 2 exact.

An initial analysis suggested that combining the raised floor with the Step 87 resolvent ceiling would force Q_C≈0 near δ*. TTCS corrected this: the ceiling B(δ) was derived under Q=0 (exact OT), and with Q>0 the modified ceiling grows faster than the floor. The derivative of the twisted ceiling with respect to Q+ is ~8.86 near (δ*,0), while the floor derivative with respect to Q_C is only 2. So the resolvent-floor combination provides no extra Q_C constraint beyond stability. This is an important negative result that prevents a false closure.

The toral black-hole coordinate equivalence reveals that the Step 90 'rapid Q redshift' is a coordinate artifact. Starting from dr²+f²dφ²+a²(dx²+dy²) and substituting φ=θ+kx reproduces the charged radial ansatz with G_xx=k²f²+a², A_θ=kf²/(k²f²+a²). At large cusp distance, α→(1/2)log(1+k²)=const, so the orbit anisotropy is just the rotated torus identification.

The curvature-energy tradeoff is a new structural observation: R(q_r)=−2σ_zz−(3/2)σ_z²−(1/2)e_s^(z), confirmed symbolically to match the Step 88 identity exactly. At a turning point H_r=0, the contracted Gauss requires R(q_r)≥6−4δ>0, but orbit energy pushes R negative. This means the flat-slice barrier and the Bochner analysis are structurally coupled: z-variation that makes slices positively curved (needed at the turning point) competes with the orbit energy that the separator floor demands. The turning point and separator are at different r-values, so this is a redistribution constraint rather than a pointwise contradiction.

A01's positive-branch result (#668) is significant: universal B_same=0 and mixed-diagonal trace obstruction Δ_tr=0.503t²>0. If the convergence ladder confirms, the mixed desingularization is perturbatively obstructed. This does not yet prove global Einstein nonexistence (non-perturbative metrics may exist), but it identifies candidate smooth 4-manifolds for the positive branch. The gap from perturbative obstruction to global nonexistence requires either a moduli-space argument or a topological exclusion.

The current negative-branch frontier is genuinely z-dependent geometry on the free cylindrical base. The established constraints — stability (Q_C≤3+δ), floor (⟨e_s⟩≥12−8δ+2Q_C), Bochner (exact OT obstruction), curvature-energy tradeoff (R(q_r) requires area concavity) — are all verified structural results, but none individually closes the gap for non-OT metrics. The decisive next question is whether the coupled (area, orbit, Maxwell, Bochner) system permits sufficient energy redistribution between the turning region and the separator for all constraints to hold simultaneously.

## Deep-Reasoning

Step 92 changed the geometry of the active negative-side route twice: first by correcting a consequential sign, then by converting the resulting separator question into both a positive estimate for charge and an exact local escape mechanism for normal orbit energy. The correct contracted Gauss identity is R_Σ = -6 + D + ℋ² - |II|². At the minimal separator ℋ = 0, one has R_Σ = -6 + D - |II|² ≤ -6 + 4δ. Thus the Step 91 interpretation requiring positive slice curvature was false, and ℋ = 0 had also been confused with ∂rℋ = 0. The exact Koiso center R_Σ = -6 already fixes the sign. The radial flat-torus barrier nevertheless survives because R_Σ = 0 implies ℋ² - |II|² = 6 - D and hence ℋ² ≥ 9 - 6δ.

The full invariant second variation of the weighted-length minimizing loop is substantially stronger than its constant test. For V = |II|² = κ² + h_ν²/2 + e_ν/2 + Q, every periodic invariant speed φ satisfies ∫ρVφ² ≤ ∫ρ[(φ_s)² + (3 - E_νν)φ²]. Combining this with R_Σ = -2h_s - 3h²/2 - e_s/2 and the corrected Gauss identity yields h_s = 3 - D/2 + V/2 - 3h²/4 - e_s/4. Conjugating by φ = ρ^(-1/2)y removes the potentially uncontrolled weight and gives the unweighted Schrödinger form ∫𝒲y² ≤ ∫[(y_s)² + a_δy²], where 𝒲 = 3V/4 + (h² + e_s)/8 and a_δ = 9/2 + 3δ/2. This supplies periodic capacity and Birman–Schwinger control independent of oscillation of ρ. The exact square-well model shows the sharp qualitative scope: stability alone permits height A tending to infinity on width ℓ tending to zero, with Aℓ approaching 2√a tanh(√aL/2). It controls concentrated mass but not height or a universal length scale.

Maxwell transport changes the charge part of that conclusion. With w = √(2Q), the tangential inequality |w_s + 3hw/2| ≤ w√e_s/2 + 2√2δ has growth coefficient c satisfying c² ≤ 5(h² + e_s)/2 ≤ 20𝒲. A local capacity estimate therefore bounds both the mass of Q near its maximum and the integrated cost required for w to rise. Direct Gronwall propagation gives a finite separator estimate sup_C Q ≤ C_Q(δ), independent of separator length and ρ-oscillation. The displayed constant is extremely coarse, approximately 6×10^10 at δ = 0, and does not become small with δ. It is nevertheless a structural advance over Q_C ≤ 3 + δ: arbitrary charge-height concentration on the separator is excluded. It cannot be substituted for the global quantity Q_+ = sup_B Q required by the twisted resolvent argument.

The strongest new understanding concerns e_ν. The apparent formal freedom to concentrate normal orbit energy is not merely a deficient collection of separator jets. For any positive analytic periodic P, choose a closed immersed curve U in H² with |U_s|² = 12 + 2P and set q = ds² + M(U(s)) on T³. If N is the target unit normal and B = √(P/2) M^(-1)dM(N) is the vertical trace-free Weingarten block, then Scal_q = -6 - P, tr W = 0, tr(W²) = P, and the only nontrivial momentum component is tr(AB) = 0 because N is perpendicular to U_s. Thus the complete Einstein Cauchy constraints for Einstein constant -3 hold exactly. Under the source Weingarten convention, U_ν = -√(2P)N and e_ν = 2P. Taking analytic von Mises spikes of fixed mass m < 2√3 tanh(√3L/2) makes -d_s² + 3 - P strictly positive for sufficiently high concentration. In this translation-invariant block metric, nonzero torus Fourier modes add kᵀM^(-1)k ≥ 0, so invariant strict stability is equivalent to full strict stability. Yet sup e_ν tends to infinity. Koiso's analytic Cauchy theorem then produces genuine local analytic metrics with Ric = -3g for every member of this family. TTCS independently verified the target normalization, momentum connection terms, Hamiltonian equation, sign of U_ν, global target normal, analyticity, Fourier-mode stability, and local Einstein conclusion.

This local escape theorem changes the worthwhile next question. No separator-local argument, even one using full stability, complete Cauchy constraints, and exact Einstein equations in a neighborhood, can bound normal orbit energy. The missing information must span a collar or use the two complete ends. The germ radius may collapse as the spike concentrates, and nothing here constructs a complete two-ended connector or proves that the central T³ globally minimizes the required essential class. The decisive object is therefore a uniform-distance transport or continuation result controlling ∫(|h_ν| + √e_ν)dn from the separator to the ends, or conversely a two-variable continuation that extends these concentrated Koiso germs into the solved expanding tails. This remains a free-T² symmetry-class problem and is far from the unrestricted Yau-26 quantifiers. Non-T² graph metrics, the N#N route, the positive normalized branch, higher dimensions, all-Einstein nonexistence on a fixed smooth manifold, and the requested Lean formalization remain unresolved.
