## Deep-Reasoning

Step 93 pursued the tubular-collar mathematics for the free-T\u00b2 charged connector, beginning from the Step 92 handoff that identified concentrated Koiso germs as a local escape mechanism requiring collar transport control. The step produced one valid structural theorem, one major corrected error, and one significant new identity that reframes the entire Q-control problem.

The deepest finding is the exact supersolution identity LQ = |\u2207Q|\u00b2/Q - 18Q - 4Q\u00b2 for the physical twist energy Q under the exact Einstein equations. This arises from a clean algebraic mechanism: the area equation L\u03c3 = 6+Q contributes -3(6+Q) = -18-3Q to the reaction, and the orbit traceless equation L\u03b1 = Q contributes -Q, giving total reaction -18-4Q. The gradient term |\u2207Q|\u00b2/Q is nonneg, so at any interior maximum (where \u2207Q=0), LQ = -18Q-4Q\u00b2 < 0 for Q > 0. The strong maximum principle then says Q achieves its maximum on the boundary. For a two-ended cylinder with Q \u2192 0 at both cusp ends, Q \u2261 0. This gives a purely differential proof of the Koiso OT theorem and the exact two-ended connector impossibility, independent of the Bochner argument of Steps 85-88.

The coefficient -18 is structurally significant. It comes from 3\u00d7(Einstein constant contribution to the area equation) + (orbit trace contribution). It is much larger than the O(\u03b4) perturbation from area/orbit defects in the forced case, suggesting that the forced maximum principle should close with a strong margin. The equivalent form L(log Q) = -18-4Q means log Q is a strict supersolution of L + 18 = 0, a much stronger condition than mere subharmonicity.

The Koiso OT theorem was established as a structural result: the Step 92 constrained Cauchy data have q = 0, and exact Einstein Maxwell conservation dq = 0 preserves q \u2261 0 throughout the germ domain. TTCS verified this reasoning, including the gauge condition F_{\u03bds}^a = 0 from the Gaussian normal gauge and the uniqueness of the Koiso continuation. The consequence is that concentrated normal orbit energy e_\u03bd at the separator does not help for exact metrics; any constructive two-ended continuation must use non-zero mixed Ricci forcing to create twist.

The signed Maxwell transport analysis corrected a critical directional error. My original argument attempted to propagate backward from the cusp end (w = 0) toward the separator, using the damping kernel exp(-(p-c)(t-r)) with p-c \u2248 3 on the cusp. TTCS decisively refuted this: the backward propagation uses the growth kernel exp((p+c)(s-r)) instead, and a 1D counterexample shows w(0) ~ \u03b2 e^{3R} when forcing is at distance R. The forward direction (separator to cusp) correctly damps: w(n) \u2264 e^{-3n}w(0) + 2\u221a2\u03b4/3, but this bounds cusp-side twist given separator twist, not the reverse. The self-consistent thresholds \u03b4** \u2248 0.186 and 0.210 were accordingly withdrawn.

The Ricci component distinction was clarified: E_ns (base normal \u00d7 base tangential) sources the Codazzi/horizontal constraint, while E_na and E_sa (base \u00d7 orbit) source the Maxwell equation. Normal twist transport is sourced specifically by E_sa, not E_ns. This corrects the Step 92 collar seed.

For the forced case, the supersolution identity becomes L(log Q) = -18 - 4Q + 2L(log q_0) - 3D_\u03c3 - D_\u03b1, where the area/orbit defects contribute at most 4\u03b4 and the charge-derivative term 2L(log q_0) involves d*S/q_0, which requires first derivatives of the Ricci defect. This is the precisely identified remaining gap. At the maximum of Q, \u2207Q = 0 constrains \u2207(log q_0) = (3\u2207\u03c3+\u2207\u03b1)/2, and the -|\u03be|\u00b2 part of L(log q_0) is favorable. A weak/integrated formulation avoiding pointwise \u2207E, or an equation-based regularity estimate for q_0, would close the forced case and give Q_max = O(\u03b4\u00b2/18).

The research connection to the full Yau-26 problem: even a complete forced Q bound would only close the free-T\u00b2 two-ended connector with complete cusp-type extensions, not general graph manifolds, non-T\u00b2 metrics, the positive branch, or higher dimensions. But the supersolution identity is a genuinely new structural result with the right quantitative strength, and it identifies the forced charge derivative as the single remaining analytic object in the T\u00b2 reduction. A01's Step 100 structural proof of same-chirality vanishing (B_{++}=B_{--}=0) for the positive-branch desingularization was absorbed; it is a finite algebraic identity from the anti-self-dual structure of EH, not a numerical observation.

## Deep-Reasoning

Step 94 replaced the false scalar maximum argument with the coupled structures that actually govern twist. For L=Δ+∇σ·∇, the diagonal fixed-charge identity LQ=|∇Q|²/Q−18Q−4Q² is algebraically correct, but at an interior maximum its negative right-hand side is compatible with LQ≤0. The even scalar solution of y″=−18−4eʸ, y′(0)=0, gives a strict positive maximum Q=eʸ at the center and Q→0 at both infinities; its first integral was numerically preserved to about 10⁻⁹. Thus the Step 93 boundary-maximum inference, its Q=O(δ²) prediction, and its purported independent recovery of the OT obstruction were withdrawn. Exact OT on an open end still forces zero charge on a connected exact Einstein region through the separate conservation law dq=0, whereas physical Q may decay to zero by redshift with nonzero conserved coordinate charge.

The fixed-charge calculation was extended invariantly to the full two-component charge and non-diagonal orbit map. For F(U)=½qᵀM(U)⁻¹q and β=log F, exact symbolic differentiation gives Hess β=h−dβ⊗dβ and |∇β|=1. Combining τσ(U)=−Q∇β, Lσ=6+Q, and Q=e^(−3σ)F(U) yields L log Q=−18−4Q+e−|d(β∘U)|². The last term is the orbit energy transverse to the horospherical charge direction and is nonnegative; it vanishes only in the charge-aligned diagonal reduction. Consequently even the sign of L log Q at a critical point is not controlled in the general fixed-charge geometry. The exact mixed Ricci law was also sharpened to e^(−3σ)M^{ab}⟨dq_a,dq_b⟩=4|E_mix|²_HS, so |b|≤2√2δ. This is the derivative-free source relation available under C⁰ Ricci pinching; logarithmic variable-charge equations are additionally singular at charge zeros.

A smooth two-ended redshift-taper family then tested whether the mixed law, both exact OT end values, the area equation, and finite separator charge could furnish global coercivity. It imposes q=0 on both outer collars, w′+(3/2)σ′w=b, and ρ″=(6+Q)ρ with Q=q²/(2ρ³), while retaining Q(0)=1/2. Delaying a fixed-width charge taper to distance R gives ||b||∞ asymptotic to exp(−3√6R/2); it fell from 3.32×10⁻² at R=1 to 3.49×10⁻¹⁰ at R=6. The weighted charge/source ratio grew as exp(2√6R), reaching 3.58×10¹². The exact first integral (ρ′)²=6ρ²−ρ⁻¹−5 explains both rates. Hence Maxwell transport, two-end charge cancellation, the exact area equation, and a finite separator Q bound cannot by themselves make Q small or produce a length-independent weighted Poincaré estimate. This family is not a reduced Einstein connector: freezing M violates the orbit equation when Q>0, and the horizontal equation is omitted. It precisely isolates the equations that must carry any remaining cost.

Local separator geometry was strengthened in the opposite direction. A charged extension of the Step 92 Koiso data was constructed. Choose 0<S<3, a periodic hyperbolic target circle with |U_s|²=12+2S, fixed nonzero charge q scaled so Q=½qᵀM⁻¹q<S, P=S−Q, vertical block B=√(P/2)M⁻¹dM(N), and mixed Weingarten covector m=−q/2 at ρ=1. The complete block endomorphism has tr W=0 and tr(W²)=P+Q=S. Its scalar curvature is −6−S; all Hamiltonian and momentum constraints hold, including cancellation of the vertical connection terms, and the full Jacobi form is ∫(|∇φ|²+(3−S)φ²). For S=1, Q ranged from 0.2405 to 0.5, the stability eigenvalue was 2, and all numerical normalization residuals were below 1.3×10⁻¹⁴. Koiso therefore gives a genuine local analytic Ric=−3g germ with nonzero conserved twist and a fully stable minimal T³. Minimality, full stability, and all local Einstein constraints do not force separator charge to vanish; the obstruction or construction must be global.

The missing horizontal relation was then derived invariantly. With H=Ric_B−Hess σ−½dσ²−½U*h−Qγ_B+3γ_B, T=Lσ−6−Q, Z=τσ(U)+∇_UQ, and m_q=e^(−3σ)⟨M⁻¹q,dq⟩, contracted Bianchi and harmonic-map stress conservation give 2 div_σ H−d tr H=−dT−T dσ−⟨Z,dU⟩−m_q. Its radial specialization is exactly C′=−2(u+h)C−wb, so the Step 90 second terminal moment is the invariant charge-work term rather than a radial accident. Testing against an end-supported vector field X gives the derivative-free pairing ∫m_q(X)dμ_σ=∫[2H:sym∇X−(tr H)div_σX+T div X−⟨Z,dU(X)⟩]dμ_σ. ## Deep-Reasoning

Step 95 pursued two connected investigations and produced one genuine new tool, one important structural correction, and a clearer landscape for the remaining free-T² connector problem.

The K_X charge-work quadratic form is a new algebraic identity connecting twist charge to horizontal defect. For A = e^{-3σ}M^{-1}, Q = ½q^TAq, the charge one-form m_q = q^TAdq satisfies ∫m_q(X)dμ_σ = -(1/2)∫q^TK_Xq dμ_σ where K_X = X(A)+(div_σX)A. Combined with the horizontal Bianchi pairing, this gives a new relation between the charge distribution and the Ricci defect blocks tested against X. The identity with X = ∇σ has a natural sign split: the coefficient k = 6+Q-3|∇σ|²-⟨∇α,∇σ⟩ is positive at the center (where Q is concentrated) and negative on the cusp (where Q is small). The area-charge coupling identities ∫Q(3|∇σ|²+⟨∇α,∇σ⟩)dμ_σ = ∫Q(6+Q)dμ_σ and ∫Q(3⟨∇α,∇σ⟩+e)dμ_σ = ∫Q²dμ_σ constrain the orbit-area-charge correlation. These identities are consistent with the K_X framework and provide additional constraints on the charge distribution.

I initially claimed that because the drift curvature Ric_f contains +Qγ, the Bochner gains +Qe which is favorable and can be dropped to recover the OT ceiling. This would have made the OT obstruction δ<0.246 apply automatically to all charged connectors. TTCS verification decisively refuted this by identifying the exact cancellation: the twist tension τ_σ = -Q∇β + Z contributes ⟨dU, D(-Q∇β)⟩ = -Qe + 3Q⟨∇σ, d(β∘U)⟩ to the Bochner. The +Qe from the drift and -Qe from the tension exactly cancel. The net twist contribution is 3Q⟨∇σ, d(β∘U)⟩ = -3Q⟨∇α,∇σ⟩ (diagonal constant charge), which has no fixed sign and depends on the orbit-area gradient correlation. I verified this cancellation symbolically. The tension estimates become |τ_σ| ≤ Q + Cδ, so the resolvent source is Q-dependent and the OT ceiling cannot be directly used.

The structural consequence is profound: the net twist Bochner contribution vanishes at both the cusp (Q→0) and the separator (|∇σ|→0), concentrating in the transition region of bounded base extent. This means the cusp behavior of the orbit energy is effectively OT regardless of twist, while the transition region accumulates the Q-dependent cost. The transition-region localization is the key new insight for the next steps.

The valid established results are: (1) K_X identity (new structural tool), (2) area-charge coupling identities, (3) exact Bochner cancellation formula, (4) separator floor ≥ 12-8δ with twist (TTCS confirmed), (5) CD(-(3+δ),4) still holds with twist. The withdrawn result is the claim that the OT ceiling applies to charged connectors. The decisive remaining question is whether Q_+ can be bounded by δ alone, exploiting the transition localization, or whether the full coupled system admits small-δ solutions with Q > 0.

For the original Yau 26 problem: the free-T² connector remains an intermediate symmetry-class investigation. Even closing the twist question would only settle free T² with two cusp-type ends, not general graph manifolds, the positive branch, higher dimensions, or the full unrestricted problem.

Step 96 replaced an excluded radial experiment with the genuinely spatially varying object inherited from the charged Koiso construction. The Step also removed two unsupported premises from the previous route: minimality of an invariant separator does not generally imply ∇σ=0, and Lσ≥6 neither bounds transition length nor lets an exterior region inherit the complete-base resolvent ceiling because entrance data remain.

The charged Koiso center was instead developed through the full s-dependent Gaussian Einstein equations. For g=dn²+q(n,s), K=q_n/2, W=q⁻¹K, and H=tr W, Ric(g)=−3g gives q_n=2K and K_n=Ric(q)+3q−HK+2Kq⁻¹K, with constraints R(q)−H²+|W|²=−6 and div K−dH=0. A general symbolic matrix calculation independently recovered the momentum equations, including the cancellation of the two vertical connection terms. From the exact center data H=0, |W|²=S, R(qΣ)=−6−S, one obtains the new pointwise Taylor structure H_n=3−S, a_nn=−3−S−Q(s), and σ_nn=6+Q(s). Thus, for 0<S<3, the strictly stable charged separator initially expands in both outward directions. For S=1 the base-circle scale contracts while orbit area expands, with their logarithmic derivatives combining to H_n=2. This explicitly identifies how the true two-variable geometry evades the flat-slice model: the separator's s-dependent orbit shape supplies intrinsic negative curvature, while charge and orbit-area response separate the horizontal and vertical expansion channels.

A Fourier method-of-lines implementation followed the exact analytic germ over a very short collar. This supports only the implementation and short analytic continuation; normal Einstein evolution is elliptically ill-posed, and no order-one collar, complete end, or two-ended connector follows.

The proposed relative K_X quantity was then evaluated on the same two-variable geometry. A load-bearing clarification emerged: for fixed coordinate charge c and compactly supported X, ½cᵀK_Xc=div_σ(QX), so its integral vanishes by algebraic integration by parts independently of the horizontal Noether identity. The computed ratio near 4.8×10⁻¹¹ is therefore a null control for charge conservation and implementation, not an obstruction or an independent verification of Noether. This explains why local choices of X cannot expose a global charge cost: a useful field must arise from an adjoint problem spanning the center and both ends, and its coefficient growth must be measured on the same degenerating geometry.

These findings motivated a precise global object. On the entire quotient cylinder, use conformal base metric γ=e^{2φ}(dτ²+ds²), orbit metric G=e^σM(U), charge q, and Coulomb-gauged connection. The complete normalized residual is (H,T,Z,B_mix), where H is the horizontal tensor, T=Lσ−6−Q, Z=τ_σ(U)+∇_UQ, and B_mix=e^{-3σ/2}M^{-1/2}dq. Charge remains a first-order conservation variable rather than an invented second-order target field. The scalar/map principal block has determinant −2|ξ|⁸; with the two first-order dq blocks, the overdetermined Gram determinant is 4|ξ|²⁰ and the generic symbol has full rank six. Thus the gauge-reduced core has an injective Douglis–Nirenberg principal symbol, while its Fredholm index, end modes, and finite cokernel remain to be determined.

An initial round-cusp indicial calculation further sharpened the next problem. For γ=y⁻²(dy²+ds²), σ=−2log y, constant U, and zero background charge, the coupled trace-horizontal/area determinant is −2λ(λ−4)(λ−3)(λ+1). The traceless horizontal equation removes the trace-only λ=4 mode, leaving scalar roots −1,0,3; the orbit-map roots are 0 and 3. The charge block has a constant-coordinate-charge mode at λ=0 whose mixed Ricci norm is redshifted by three powers of y, while its horizontal contribution Q is quadratic and redshifted by six powers. This supplies a concrete analytic origin for a possible end-escaping near-kernel, but not its compatibility with the charged center or both ends.

The resulting scientific picture is more focused. The charged center is locally compatible with exact Einstein geometry, strict stability, nonzero twist, and initial two-sided expansion, so no separator-local theorem can exclude the connector. Conversely, exact fixed charge cannot terminate in an exact orthogonally transitive open set without mixed Ricci forcing. The decisive issue is a shared-parameter global matching problem: can the same center parameters feed two expanded regions and then discharge charge while every Ricci block tends to zero, or does the full adjoint cokernel impose a length-independent nonzero moment? The relevant independent projections are vector charge flux, connection holonomy, weighted TT/Hopf tensors, global Noether fields, and the three target-Killing currents. This remains a restricted free-T² negative-side mechanism and does not yet produce a closed no-Einstein manifold, settle the positive sign branch, cover nonsymmetric geometry or higher dimensions, or justify Lean formalization of Yau 26.

## Deep-Reasoning

Step 97 produced a structural breakthrough in understanding the free-T² connector problem for the negative branch of Yau 26. The central discovery is the **orbit-shape conformal dilution mechanism**: for a trial metric of the form q(n,s)=cosh²(n)·q₀(s) on the quotient cylinder, the Raychaudhuri equation H'+|W|²=3 is satisfied exactly (H=3tanh(n)), while the tangential Ricci residual E_T=Ric(q₀)+2sech²(n)·q decays at rate e^{-2n}. This was verified numerically with fitted decay rate 1.9745≈2.0 and perfect agreement between the analytic formula and the full numerical Ricci computation.

The mechanism operates through a simple but powerful principle: in an expanding geometry where the metric grows as cosh²(n), the s-derivatives of the orbit shape α₀(s) are diluted by the conformal factor. The 3D Ricci contribution Ric(q₀) is constant in n, but its operator norm q⁻¹Ric(q₀) decays as cosh⁻²(n)≈4e⁻²ⁿ because the inverse metric shrinks. The additional 2sech²(n)·q term from the Raychaudhuri-compatible Weingarten also decays at rate e⁻²ⁿ. Together, the total operator-norm defect drops from 9.25 at n=0 to 0.012 at n=4 and 0.0002 at n=6.

This discovery has profound implications for the connector construction. Previous steps (85-96) established that exact OT connectors are obstructed by the Bochner/resolvent mechanism, and that charged connectors face exact cancellations in the twist tension. The present finding shows that the orbit-shape transition—previously thought to require forced adiabatic decay at cost O(|α₀|/K) per unit length—is actually handled for free by the expanding geometry. The orbit shape can be maintained at full amplitude throughout the connector, with its Ricci contribution naturally suppressed by the conformal dilution.

The step also identified the Hamiltonian constraint as the key structural connection between the Koiso center and the expanding regime. At a minimal center (H=0) with Weingarten energy |W|²=S, the Hamiltonian requires R(q₀)=-6-S, which demands a curved T³ separator. The backbone ODE (σ''=6-σ'²-uσ', u'=3-u²-σ'u) with flat-T³ initial conditions gives σ''(0)=6 and u'(0)=3, yielding H'(0)=9—but Raychaudhuri demands H'(0)=3-S. This 6+S mismatch is precisely the orbit-shape curvature contribution to the tangential Einstein equations. The cosh²(n) trial resolves this by satisfying Raychaudhuri exactly while leaving the orbit curvature as a controlled exponentially-decaying tangential residual.

The remaining gap is the center-to-expansion connection. The cosh²(n)·q₀ trial has H(0)=0 and |W|²(0)=0, but the Koiso center has |W|²=S with off-diagonal Weingarten from the charge. The Hamiltonian deficit at n=0 is 5.1 (R(q₀)=-0.9 vs required -6). This mismatch reflects the difference between the pure diagonal orbit metric q₀ and the full Koiso separator metric with connection and curved-orbit-path curvature. To close this gap, either: (1) the Koiso analytic germ must be continued from the center past the Gaussian conjugate point (n≈0.47 for the base-circle collapse) into the expanding regime, where it hands off to the cosh² decay; or (2) a modified trial in harmonic/conformal gauge must interpolate between the exact Koiso center and the cosh² regime without coordinate singularities.

For the full Yau 26 problem, this mechanism is specific to the free-T² negative branch. The positive branch requires different manifold families and Einstein obstructions. Higher dimensions lack the specific four-dimensional topology. And even completing the negative-branch free-T² connector would need to be embedded in a closed graph manifold with certified all-sign Einstein nonexistence. The orbit-shape dilution mechanism is a significant structural advance, but it addresses only one component of a multi-component problem.

## Deep-Reasoning

Step 98 replaced the Step 97 interpretation with the actual nonlinear matching problem. The warped metric g=dn²+cosh²(n)qΣ has E_nn=E_nT=0 and E_T^sharp=sech²(n)(Ric(qΣ)^sharp+2I), but this is only an exterior benchmark: its maximum defect occurs at the waist, K(0)=0, and it cannot retain the charged Koiso Weingarten tensor. On T³ it cannot approach zero defect within this class, since ||Ric(qΣ)^sharp+2I||<2/3 would make every three-dimensional sectional curvature negative, contradicting Preissmann. The Step 97 diagonal extraction also removed genuine orbit-matrix and mixed geometry, omitted the Codazzi block, and used a coordinate rather than metric operator norm. Its orbit roots 0 and -2, conjugate-point interpretation, and coordinate-repair conclusion were therefore withdrawn. The full cusp orbit equation has radial roots 0 and -3, minimality does not force U_n=0, and loss of positivity of a quadratic Taylor truncation says nothing about continuation of the exact Einstein germ.

The new representation keeps the complete constrained center. With q0(s), K0(s) from the charged Koiso data, S0=q0^(1/2), A=S0^(-1)K0S0^(-1), and Rhat=S0^(-1)Ric(q0)S0^(-1), each half-cylinder is represented by q=S0 exp(X) S0. The center conditions X=0, X_r=±2A, and X_rr=2(Rhat+3I) give q_r=±2K0 and q_rr=2(Ric(q0)+3q0+2K0q0^(-1)K0). The second derivative follows from d²exp(X)/dr² at X=0 being X_rr+X_r²; no commutativity assumption is used, and the sign disappears in X_r². Analytic jet residuals are below 8.6e-14. Matrix exponentiation preserves positive definiteness and retains all orbit and mixed directions.

All ten components of E=Ric+3g were assembled in Gaussian coordinates: E_rr=3-tr(q^(-1)K_r)+tr(W²), E_ri=q^{jk}∇_jK_ki-∂_iH, and E_ij=Ric(q)_ij+3q_ij-(K_r)_ij-HK_ij+2(Kq^(-1)K)_ij. Cholesky conjugation E_orth=L^(-1)EL^(-T), where g=LL^T, gives the generalized eigenvalues of Ev=λgv and hence the invariant pinching norm. A flat-slice hyperbolic test q=e^(2r)I has residual below 4.2e-12 in the principal run. Independent TTCS derivations confirmed these formulas, the noncommutative center jet, and the norm implementation.

The first outer attachment q=e^(2r)q0 is not exactly Einstein. Its residual is E_rr=E_ri=0 and E_ij=Ric(q0)_ij, so its invariant size is e^(-2R)||q0^(-1/2)Ric(q0)q0^(-1/2)||. The computed endpoint values 1.0741905 at R=1 and 0.0534808 at R=2.5 have ratio e^(-3), exactly as this formula predicts. This term must either be retained explicitly or removed by matching to an expanding constant flat T³ metric.

The constrained center supplied a sharp numerical resolution test. Its analytic residual vanishes, while the discrete Codazzi block decreases with Ns as 1.3634, 0.7084, 0.3289, 0.07121, 0.01212, 3.04e-4, and 6.76e-6 for Ns=16,24,32,48,64,96,128. E_rr and E_T remain at roundoff. Thus coarse whole-grid maxima at the center are Fourier underresolution, not geometric lower bounds.

A single quintic joining the exact center jets to the expanding attachment stays positive but creates a large inner tangential residual: at Ns=64, nr=35, R=2.5 the positive and negative halves have suprema 970.66 and 99.57. Restricted full-matrix corrections reduce this only partially. A more flexible direct nodal experiment at nr=11, Ns=16, R=1 lowered the two interior packed residual norms from 260.21 to 8.90 and from 137.10 to 8.22, with joint norm 294.12 to 12.12 and monotone decrease along the saved coarse-grid update. This demonstrates discrete compensability by genuine full-matrix directions, but it does not establish a continuous connector. The optimizer stopped after four evaluations; the coefficients were not saved for refinement; nonlinear products were not dealiased; the regularizer was non-negligible; and, most importantly, the nodal field did not analytically preserve endpoint derivatives—the evaluator overwrote q_r and q_rr at endpoint rows. The apparent final supremum 1.3634 is exactly the Ns=16 center Codazzi error. TTCS independently identified these same sources of false confidence.

The resulting mathematical question is now precise. Exact local Koiso solvability already explains why sufficiently flexible fields can suppress residual near the center. What matters is whether one resolution-continuable field can preserve the shared charged center, satisfy both attachments, and keep every Ricci block small throughout a finite inner transition. A continuous obstruction would appear as a low-frequency adjoint field that persists under refinement and interval continuation, remains centered rather than following the cutoff, and pairs nontrivially with the residual after shared center and end parameters are included. Conversely, useful construction evidence requires independent fine-grid decay, coefficient-tail decay, uniform positivity, and small residual projections relative to the physical inverse scales. No such limiting behavior has yet been established.

This remains a restricted free-T² negative-side laboratory. It has not produced a connector, a small-defect sequence on a closed no-Einstein manifold, a positive-side result, a higher-dimensional result, or a Lean formalization of Yau 26.

## Deep-Reasoning

Step 99 produced three structural advances for the free-T² connector problem in Yau 26, with the Chern–Gauss–Bonnet Ricci pinching obstruction being the most consequential.

**Raychaudhuri normal-block floor.** The identity H'+H²/3+|W°|²=3−E_rr, integrated against cosh²(r) from a minimal center H(0)=0 to an expanding end H(R)=3, gives the exact weighted projection: ∫₀ᴿcosh²r(−E_rr)dr = 3cosh²R(1−tanh R) + ∫₀ᴿcosh²r[|W°|²+u²/3]dr, where u=H−3tanh r. The comparison ODE forces 1≤k·tanh(kR) with k=√(1+δ/3), giving δ_min(R)~12e^{-2R}. This was verified numerically with residual 3.4×10⁻³. Key implication: radius continuation is mathematically necessary to achieve small normal cost; fixed-R refinement cannot drive δ below δ_min(R).

**Tangential block dominance and cost structure.** The quintic jet-preserving transition on [0,1] was decomposed into all five contributing terms of E_T. Spatial curvature Ric(q) of the intermediate trial metrics dominates (peak 21.4), followed by −K_r (11.9), −HK (9.8), and 2Kq⁻¹K (9.6); the total ET peak is 28.7, three times the normal block Enn=10.7. Optimization of X(r_t) by Nelder-Mead gives only 1.2× improvement; additional radial perturbation modes give negligible further reduction. The segmented construction (inner quintic + exact expanding exterior) confirmed that the inner transition dominates the whole-cylinder residual and gets worse with longer transition lengths. The conformal expansion q=cosh²(r)q₀ provides the benchmark tangential cost: E_T = sech²(r)(Ric(q₀)^♯+2I), with operator norm 9.94 at center, decaying at rate e^{-2r}. This benchmark doesn't match the Koiso center jets but shows the irreducible orbit-shape tangential cost.

TTCS verification confirmed: no tangential Raychaudhuri analog exists (the traceless Weingarten evolution has no positive-definite integrand), but E_T≡0 implies the full E≡0 by contracted Bianchi identity with constraint propagation. Therefore any finite-R connector must have E_T≠0 somewhere, and an exact Einstein metric with H(0)=0 satisfies H<3tanh r, so it cannot reach H(R)=3 at finite R.

**Chern–Gauss–Bonnet Ricci pinching floor.** The most significant result: on any closed oriented 4-manifold with χ=0, the Chern–Gauss–Bonnet identity ∫|Ric°|²=2∫|W|²+(1/12)∫s² with |W|²≥0, combined with the pointwise bounds |Ric°|²≤4δ² and |s|≥4(|Λ|−δ), gives δ≥|Λ|/(1+√3). For Λ=−3: δ≥3(√3−1)/2≈1.098. This is a universal, normalization-dependent, and dimension-specific constraint. It applies to graph manifolds, free-T² manifolds, and surface bundles with χ=0. The connector-cusps absorption analysis shows that (4δ²−(4/3)(3−δ)²)Vol_conn≥12Vol_cusps, and the coefficient vanishes at exactly δ=1.098, confirming that the floor is sharp at |W|=0. Any connector as part of a closed χ=0 manifold must have δ_conn>1.098 strictly.

This changes the research target fundamentally: the connector need NOT achieve δ→0; the target is δ≈1.098. The current quintic gives 28.7, so there is still a 26× gap, but the problem is now finite-target matching rather than asymptotic convergence. The conformal benchmark reaches the CGB level at r≈1.72; the Koiso germ continuation (estimated r_max~0.7–0.8) must therefore be supplemented by a better transition mechanism to bridge [r_max, 1.72].

The CGB floor also constrains the Yau-26 negative branch: for χ=0 manifolds, no metric can satisfy c₄g≤Ric≤C₄g with C₄/c₄<√3/(2+√3)≈0.464 (negative case). This means the universal interval must be at least [−4.098, −1.902] to be non-vacuous on graph manifolds. For manifolds with χ>0 (surface bundles, hyperbolic manifolds), the CGB floor weakens or disappears, so the counterexample strategy depends critically on which manifold class is targeted.

The connection between the CGB floor and the earlier Chern–Weil obstruction of Step 2 (2χ>3|τ| for tight near-Einstein metrics) is now explicit: both use the same CGB identity, but the χ=0 application gives a universal pointwise floor rather than a topological inequality. The earlier observation that 'Weyl curvature does not provide a way around' the CGB obstruction on T⁴ is confirmed and generalized to all χ=0 manifolds with a specific numerical constant.

## Deep-Reasoning

Step 100 restored the quantifiers that govern the entire Yau 26 program. A negative-branch disproof in dimension four requires no-Einstein manifolds with normalized defect ‖Ric+3g‖op tending to zero; a single metric with defect near 1.098 cannot defeat an existential interval that may be arbitrarily narrower. The closed χ=0 lower bound therefore cannot become a finite construction target. Even a successful negative sequence would address only P₄⁻; complete negation of Q₄=P₄⁺∨P₄⁻ would also require failure of P₄⁺ in the same dimension, though the two sequences may use different manifolds.

The topological premise behind Step 99's connector argument was also repaired. A local free-T² connector has toral ends but does not induce a global free torus action after gluing. Pure finite-volume real-hyperbolic four-pieces have positive Euler characteristic, with Vol₋₁(P)=4π²χ(P)/3, and gluing along flat three-manifolds preserves the sum of their Euler characteristics. Imposing the closed χ=0 formula on the connector deleted precisely this hyperbolic contribution. The value 3(√3−1)/2 was already the Step 2/64 lower bound for closed four-manifolds with nonpositive Euler characteristic, and equating separate scalar and trace-free Ricci estimates did not establish geometric attainment or sharpness.

The useful replacement is an exact relative Chern–Gauss–Bonnet identity. If N is the union of regions replacing exact hyperbolic cusp tails of total volume Vrem, the complement remains sectional-curvature −1, VN=Vol(N), and E=Ric+3g with e=tr E, then
2∫N|W|²+12(VN−Vrem)=∫N(|E°|²+2e−e²/12).
For Ricci eigenvalue errors xi∈[−δ,δ], the quadratic part is Σxi²−(Σxi)²/3, whose absolute value is at most 4δ², while |2Σxi|≤8δ. Hence the absolute left side is at most (8δ+4δ²)VN. A vanishing-defect sequence must therefore satisfy Vrem−VN=(1/6)∫N|W|²+o(VN). This is a genuine global compatibility relation: volume deficit pays for Weyl energy. It is not automatically obstructive because VN may be smaller than Vrem, and satisfying it does not solve the horizontal, shape, or charge equations.

An explicit pure-piece laboratory was identified from the Ratcliffe–Tschantz one-cusped 24-cell manifolds. The orientable double cover 24cdc1.1 has one T³ cusp, χ=2, hyperbolic volume 8π²/3, maximum-cusp volume 16, b₁=1, and b₃=0. Thus the cusp-section inclusion has positive rational H₁ image, closing the old Step 70 peripheral-rank question for this piece. A primitive character nonzero on the cusp group yields, for degrees N coprime to its peripheral multiplicity, one-cusp cyclic covers with peripheral type (N,1,1). Two such pieces can be paired through an orientation-compatible affine torus gluing to form the intended pure-piece graph family, subject to direct verification of the precise Di Cerbo hypotheses and gluing data.

For each fixed dimensionless connector profile, a degree-N cusp cover truncated at T=log N+T₀ has interface three-volume and removed-tail volume proportional to N⁻². The rank-two quotient of the charged Koiso connector is locally isometric before quotienting and likewise multiplies connector volume, Weyl energy, and every local defect integral by N⁻². The executable calculation verifies this common scaling to relative spread below 2.3×10⁻¹⁵. Consequently lattice collapse alone creates neither a contradiction nor a construction: after division by connector volume, the relative Chern–Gauss–Bonnet equation is independent of N. In the actual vanishing-defect regime the half-length R must also tend to infinity; isotropic endpoint expansion changes the matching depth to T=log N−R+O(1), so one must choose N much larger than e^R and retain the R-dependent dimensionless volumes. This joint asymptotic relation is the next global refinement.

The corrected global bridge strengthens the research without replacing the unresolved center-to-expansion problem. It supplies a precise observable that can distinguish a persistent geometric mismatch from a poor interpolant, while the current evidence shows no such mismatch. The faithful full-matrix construction still needs a resolution-continuable transition with complete Ricci defect tending to zero, and the positive branch and Lean formalization remain independent unfinished parts of the highest goal.
