- Exact Maxwell conservation kills twist on an exact Einstein connected open end, but an approximately Einstein interior can carry sourced charge despite exact cusp ends. Thus twist is not eliminated by end asymptotics alone. Radial charged cylindrical controls were abandoned because every radial \(T^3\) slice remains intrinsically flat; contracted Gauss forces a large mean curvature and prevents a small-defect passage from negative to positive expansion. Genuine charged constructions must be \(s\)-dependent and use nonflat orbit geometry [Steps 90-96].

- Charged Koiso separators show that local constraints do not force charge to vanish. Full Hamiltonian and momentum constraints, strict stability, minimality, and local analytic Einstein evolution can coexist with concentrated orbit energy and nonzero conserved twist. The relevant unresolved object is therefore global: a two-ended charged throat, or a global adjoint identity preventing one [Steps 92-96].

- The horizontal Bianchi/Noether identity and the \(K_X\) charge-work form were retained as global diagnostics:
  \[
  2\operatorname{div}_\sigma H-d\operatorname{tr}H
  =-dT-Td\sigma-\langle Z,dU\rangle-m_q,
  \]
  together with the charge-work quadratic form involving
  \[
  K_X=X(A)+(\operatorname{div}_\sigma X)A.
  \]
  Compactly supported fixed-charge tests can vanish algebraically, so a useful obstruction requires a global adjoint spanning the center and both ends, with parameter normalization and inverse scales controlled on the degenerating geometry [Steps 94-96].

- The numerical/matching representation was corrected to preserve the full geometry: \(q=S_0\exp(X)S_0\), rather than diagonal extraction. Exact charged center jets, all Gaussian Ricci blocks, and invariant operator norms must be retained. Earlier diagonal scripts, coordinate norms, omitted Codazzi blocks, wrong radial roots, and positivity-loss interpretations were withdrawn [Steps 97-98].

- Coarse full-matrix matching reduced discrete residuals but did not establish a construction. Endpoint derivatives were overwritten, coefficients were not saved for refinement, de-aliasing and regularization were inadequate, and center maxima reflected Fourier underresolution. Valid evidence requires resolution-continuable fields, field-derived endpoint jets, fine-grid reevaluation, coefficient-tail decay, positivity margins, and residual projections measured against physical inverse scales [Step 98].

- Raychaudhuri supplies a necessary normal-cost diagnostic, not a global theorem. For an outward Gaussian half with \(\mathcal H(0)=0\), \(\mathcal H(R)=3\),
  \[
  \mathcal H'=3-\mathcal H^2/3-|W^\circ|^2-E_{rr},
  \]
  so fixed \(R\) imposes a defect floor \(1\le k\tanh(kR)\), \(k=\sqrt{1+\delta/3}\); small defect requires \(R\to\infty\). The weighted normal residual identity separates compulsory endpoint cost from shear and mean-curvature mismatch, while current trials remain tangential-block dominated [Step 99].

- Step 100 withdrew the proposed universal \(\chi=0\) connector floor and the finite-target route near \(\delta=3(\sqrt3-1)/2\approx1.098\). The closed \(\chi=0\) Chern–Gauss–Bonnet estimate itself is valid in its scope, but the connector has boundary and the completed real-hyperbolic graph manifold need not have \(\chi=0\) or a global free torus action. For pure hyperbolic-piece graphs, \(\chi(M)>0\) is supplied by the hyperbolic pieces, and gluing along torus boundaries preserves their Euler-characteristic contribution. The claimed sharpness was also withdrawn because separate scalar and traceless-Ricci bounds need not be simultaneously attained [Step 100].

- The corrected global bridge is a relative Chern–Gauss–Bonnet budget. If \(N\) replaces exact hyperbolic cusp tails of total removed volume \(V_{\mathrm{removed}}\), the complement is sectional curvature \(-1\), and \(E=\mathrm{Ric}+3g\), then
  \[
  2\int_N|W|^2+12\bigl(\mathrm{Vol}(N)-V_{\mathrm{removed}}\bigr)
  =
  \int_N\left(|E^\circ|^2+2\operatorname{tr}E-\frac{(\operatorname{tr}E)^2}{12}\right).
  \]
  Under \(\|E\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta\), the right side has absolute value at most \((8\delta+4\delta^2)\mathrm{Vol}(N)\). This is a necessary global compatibility relation, not an obstruction by itself: volume deficit may pay for Weyl energy, and the horizontal/shape/charge equations remain unresolved [Step 100].

- The explicit graph laboratory was narrowed to orientable one-cusped real-hyperbolic four-manifolds, especially the cited Ratcliffe–Tschantz orientable double cover \(24\mathrm{cdc}1.1\), recorded with one \(T^3\) cusp, \(\chi=2\), volume \(8\pi^2/3\), maximum cusp volume \(16\), \(b_1=1\), and \(b_3=0\). A primitive character nonzero on the cusp group can yield a coprime cyclic-cover subsequence of peripheral type \((N,1,1)\); two copies may then be paired by an orientation-compatible affine torus gluing, subject to direct verification of the precise all-Einstein exclusion hypotheses and gluing data [Step 100].

- Fixed-profile lattice scaling was shown to be neutral rather than decisive. For a degree-\(N\) cusp cover truncated at \(T=\log N+T_0\), interface volume and removed-tail volume scale like \(N^{-2}\). A rank-two quotient of a fixed Koiso connector scales its volume, Weyl energy, and defect integrals by the same \(N^{-2}\). Numerical scaling checks found relative spread below \(2.3\times10^{-15}\), but the connector densities in that run were placeholders, not measured curvature data. In the actual \(\delta\to0\) regime, the half-length \(R\) must also grow and the matching depth becomes \(T=\log N-R+O(1)\), requiring \(N\gg e^R\). The \(R\)-dependent dimensionless quantities, not the common lattice factor, determine compatibility [Step 100].

### Research Line

The project began by preserving the exact quantifiers of Yau Problem 26 and separating positive, negative, and low-dimensional regimes. Early explorations of flexibility, high-frequency perturbations, ALE/desingularization, Min–Oo-type limits, and sectional pinching did not produce a same-manifold theorem or counterexample. They established the lasting standard that local curvature manipulation or exclusion of one Einstein candidate cannot answer the problem [Steps 1-2, 10, 62-64].

The first deep negative line used four-dimensional topology. Ishida–LeBrun manifolds offered all-Einstein exclusion, while mixed scalar–Weyl inequalities suggested that a near-Einstein sequence would have to collapse in a way retaining topological density. This led to the transported-cutoff Ricci-flow program. Repeated review transformed it from a naive localized estimate scheme into a technically careful regularized, weighted, all-order continuation architecture. It remains a valuable restricted theorem candidate but does not provide fixed-width Ricci-pinched no-Einstein manifolds or dimension-only constants [Steps 2-61].

The research then moved to graph manifolds because their topology supplies the stronger all-Einstein obstruction. A potential cheap entropy gap failed at equality, so the line shifted to constructing or obstructing a small-defect graph metric. Surface bundles supplied explicit slow-interpolation metrics but lacked known all-Einstein exclusion; graph manifolds supplied exclusion but lacked small-defect metrics. This complementary mismatch became the central negative-branch bottleneck [Steps 64-69].

The graph construction was decomposed into hyperbolic cusp tails, anisotropic lattice quotients, Koiso centers, and a finite core connector. The expanding tail and scale-matching quotient are understood. Exact flat, diagonal, constant-exit, and highly symmetric core models were ruled out or narrowed. The full OT formulation, slice balances, and orbit-energy quantity \(K\) clarified that center data initially have excessive orbit energy and must undergo a nonlinear turnover before expansion can return. Exact OT and free-OT complete two-ended geometries with low defect were then obstructed by weighted Bochner/resolvent and minimal-separator arguments [Steps 69-88].

This forced attention onto charged, non-OT, genuinely two-variable connectors. Maxwell transport, target-space twist geometry, horizontal Noether identities, and charged Koiso data showed both the available mechanisms and their limits. Local charged caps and stable separators exist, but radial cylindrical controls fail because of the flat-slice Gauss barrier. The unresolved object is a global two-ended charged throat with small full operator Ricci defect, or a global adjoint obstruction that survives all center/end parameters [Steps 89-96].

Numerical work was repaired accordingly. Full positive-definite orbit matrices, exact center jets, all Gaussian Ricci blocks, invariant norms, and resolution checks replaced diagonal or coordinate-level experiments. Current coarse matching reduces discrete residuals but has not shown a convergent family; tangential curvature and Weingarten-evolution errors dominate. Raychaudhuri gives a necessary radius continuation and normal-cost benchmark, but no tangential monotonicity principle has been found [Steps 97-99].

Step 100 restored the global topology and quantifier bridge after the erroneous finite-\(\delta\) interpretation. The closed \(\chi=0\) floor cannot be imposed on a boundary connector or treated as a finite counterexample target. Instead, relative Chern–Gauss–Bonnet compares the connector’s Weyl energy and volume deficit with the exact hyperbolic cusp volume it replaces. An explicit one-cusped hyperbolic-piece laboratory and common \(N^{-2}\) scaling were identified, but no persistent mismatch appeared. The next faithful continuation is therefore to compute the full \(R\)-dependent relative budget for a verified graph gluing using actual full-matrix curvature, Weyl energy, volume quadrature, endpoint data, and independently refined grids. If the budget remains compatible, effort returns to the unresolved joint inner transition rather than to the withdrawn \(1.098\) target [Step 100].

The positive branch remains independent and unresolved. Kähler, product, and finite-dimensional desingularization observations provide only restricted algebraic or deformation-sector information; they do not prove that a candidate smooth manifold carries no Einstein metric of any sign. Higher-dimensional obstruction mechanisms, \(S^3\)-neck constructions, surface-bundle routes, nonsymmetric graph metrics, and Lean formalization remain unfinished. No complete proof, disproof, dimension-only constants, fixed-dimensional two-sign counterexample, or formal verification has been obtained [Steps 73-100].
